eclipse-phase.rule.seeker-and-grenade-tr.go_wrong: Timed explosives may be discovered and neutralized.
eclipse-phase.rule.seeker-and-grenade-tr.who_may: Munition user; wireless changes are possible.
eclipse-phase.rule.seeker-and-grenade-tr.combines: Wireless signal triggers require the assigned cryptographic key.
eclipse-phase.rule.seeker-and-grenade-tr.blocked_reason: The trigger conditions can be implemented as ordinary delayed or triggered effects.

eclipse-phase.rule.armor-value.name: Armor Value

effect.summary: Subtract the appropriate energy or kinetic armor from incoming damage; armor-piercing halves armor.

eclipse-phase.rule.armor-value.cost_or_limit: Use the rating matching the attack's damage type.
eclipse-phase.rule.armor-value.combines: Armor may be layered, subject to penalties.
eclipse-phase.rule.armor-value.blocked_reason: Subtraction and armor reduction fit the basic effect model.

eclipse-phase.rule.layering-armor.name: Layering Armor

effect.summary: Armor layers add their ratings but impose physical penalties and can restrict movement when too heavy.

eclipse-phase.rule.layering-armor.cost_or_limit: Each additional layer penalizes physical actions; exceeding SOM reduces movement, and exceeding Durability prevents movement.
eclipse-phase.rule.layering-armor.combines: A shell's inherent armor counts as the first layer; bonus armor marked with plus signs avoids counting as a layer.
eclipse-phase.rule.layering-armor.blocked_reason: It is a direct equipment and movement restriction.

eclipse-phase.rule.armor-visibility.name: Armor Visibility

effect.summary: High armor ratings are obvious; lower ratings are generally concealable.

eclipse-phase.rule.armor-visibility.cost_or_limit: Armor value 11 or more draws attention; concealable armor gains a hiding bonus except for conspicuous gear.
eclipse-phase.rule.armor-visibility.combines: Some bulky or activated items remain obvious.
eclipse-phase.rule.armor-visibility.blocked_reason: A visibility threshold is a simple detection modifier.

eclipse-phase.rule.adjusting-blast-radiu.name: Adjusting Blast Radius

effect.summary: A user can reduce a munition's blast radius, adjusting damage reduction for centered blasts.

eclipse-phase.rule.adjusting-blast-radiu.cost_or_limit: Requires a quick action; centered effects may increase damage falloff to a stated maximum.
eclipse-phase.rule.adjusting-blast-radiu.blocked_reason: The rule depends on spatial blast areas and distance-based damage.

eclipse-phase.rule.jumping-on-grenades.name: Jumping on Grenades

effect.summary: A nearby character can cover a grenade to reduce its damage to others.

eclipse-phase.rule.jumping-on-grenades.cost_or_limit: Requires movement range, a complex action, and a successful reflex check; the jumper takes extra damage.
eclipse-phase.rule.jumping-on-grenades.go_wrong: The jumper suffers additional damage when it detonates.
eclipse-phase.rule.jumping-on-grenades.combines: Reduces damage to others by the jumper's armor plus ten.
eclipse-phase.rule.jumping-on-grenades.blocked_reason: The rule divides an area blast's damage among targets.

eclipse-phase.rule.sticky-coating.name: Sticky Coating

effect.summary: Adhesive munitions that hit do not scatter and can be attached to an opponent for later detonation.

eclipse-phase.rule.sticky-coating.cost_or_limit: Requires a hit; attachment to an opponent requires a successful melee attack.
eclipse-phase.rule.sticky-coating.blocked_reason: Attachment and delayed use are basic interaction rules.

eclipse-phase.rule.throwing-back-a-grena.name: Throwing Back A Grenade

effect.summary: A nearby character may catch a grenade and throw it elsewhere before detonation.

eclipse-phase.rule.throwing-back-a-grena.cost_or_limit: Requires movement range, a complex action, and a reflex check at a penalty; the throw is also penalized.
eclipse-phase.rule.throwing-back-a-grena.go_wrong: Failure may leave the character at the detonation point.
eclipse-phase.rule.throwing-back-a-grena.combines: Throwing uses a standard ranged attack.
eclipse-phase.rule.throwing-back-a-grena.blocked_reason: It is a conventional action and attack check.

eclipse-phase.rule.weapon-gear-traits.name: Weapon/Gear Traits

effect.summary: Weapon and gear traits define effects such as armor piercing, blindness, entangling, knockdown, shock, stun, and handling limits.

eclipse-phase.rule.weapon-gear-traits.cost_or_limit: Each trait applies its own stated checks, modifiers, or use restriction.
eclipse-phase.rule.weapon-gear-traits.go_wrong: Some failures cause blindness, incapacitation, or other harmful results.
eclipse-phase.rule.weapon-gear-traits.mind: Pain traits can compel biomorphs to flee.
eclipse-phase.rule.weapon-gear-traits.who_may: Applies to users and targets of listed equipment.
eclipse-phase.rule.weapon-gear-traits.combines: Anti-glare ware counters light-based blinding; pain-tolerance traits reduce or negate pain effects.
eclipse-phase.rule.weapon-gear-traits.blocked_reason: Some conditions, such as compelled fleeing, require additional condition mechanics.

eclipse-phase.rule.armor-mods.name: Armor Mods

effect.summary: Only one armor modification may be applied at a time; temporary coatings last one day.

eclipse-phase.rule.armor-mods.cost_or_limit: Permanent coatings require a specialized hive; most mods are visible.
eclipse-phase.rule.armor-mods.go_wrong: Limited-use coatings lose charges when activated or struck.
eclipse-phase.rule.armor-mods.combines: Mods can be applied to clothing, armor, skin, or shell.
eclipse-phase.rule.armor-mods.blocked_reason: Some modifications have charge depletion and repair limits.

eclipse-phase.rule.area-effect-attacks.name: Area-Effect Attacks

effect.summary: Area attacks are centered blasts, cones, or uniform blasts, with different target and damage patterns.

eclipse-phase.rule.area-effect-attacks.cost_or_limit: Blast damage decreases with distance; space reduces explosive damage because there is no atmosphere.
eclipse-phase.rule.area-effect-attacks.go_wrong: A successful partial defense may still leave half damage.
eclipse-phase.rule.area-effect-attacks.who_may: Attackers and targets of area effects.
eclipse-phase.rule.area-effect-attacks.combines: Fray and cover can avoid or reduce damage; attack type determines affected targets.
eclipse-phase.rule.area-effect-attacks.blocked_reason: The rules require area geometry, distance, and multi-target resolution.

eclipse-phase.rule.scatter.name: Scatter

effect.summary: A missed area attack lands in a random direction and distance, then its blast is resolved normally.

eclipse-phase.rule.scatter.cost_or_limit: Roll a ten-sided die; each superior failure doubles the distance.
eclipse-phase.rule.scatter.go_wrong: The attack may land among unintended targets.
eclipse-phase.rule.scatter.combines: Microgravity may require an additional orientation roll.
eclipse-phase.rule.scatter.blocked_reason: It requires spatial placement and area resolution.

eclipse-phase.rule.attacks-against-the-h.name: Attacks Against the Helpless

effect.summary: An attack test against a helpless target outside combat kills on success; failure inflicts maximum damage.

eclipse-phase.rule.attacks-against-the-h.cost_or_limit: Requires time to line up the attack; does not apply during combat action turns.
eclipse-phase.rule.attacks-against-the-h.go_wrong: A failed test still inflicts maximum damage.
eclipse-phase.rule.attacks-against-the-h.blocked_reason: It is a direct attack-resolution rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.blind-attacks.name: Blind Attacks

effect.summary: A sensed but unseen target is attacked at a penalty; failure to perceive also gives the attack a chance to miss automatically.

eclipse-phase.rule.blind-attacks.cost_or_limit: Attack penalty applies in either case; failed perception adds a 50% miss chance.
eclipse-phase.rule.blind-attacks.who_may: A character unable to see the target.
eclipse-phase.rule.blind-attacks.combines: Other senses can be used to perceive.
eclipse-phase.rule.blind-attacks.blocked_reason: It uses ordinary perception and attack checks.

eclipse-phase.rule.called-shots.name: Called Shots

effect.summary: A penalized attack can aim for armor gaps, disarm, knock down, redirect, or strike a specific location.

eclipse-phase.rule.called-shots.cost_or_limit: Declared before the attack; area-effect attacks cannot use called shots.
eclipse-phase.rule.called-shots.go_wrong: A non-superior hit merely strikes normally.
eclipse-phase.rule.called-shots.who_may: An attacker making a single-target attack.
eclipse-phase.rule.called-shots.combines: Superior successes enable the chosen special outcome.
eclipse-phase.rule.called-shots.blocked_reason: Specific component disablement and redirect outcomes need additional target-state rules.

eclipse-phase.rule.coated-weapons.name: Coated Weapons

effect.summary: A coated melee weapon delivers one dose of a compatible drug or toxin on its next damaging hit.

eclipse-phase.rule.coated-weapons.cost_or_limit: Only one dose at a time; only dermal or injection agents can be applied.
eclipse-phase.rule.coated-weapons.go_wrong: A critical failure doses the wielder.
eclipse-phase.rule.coated-weapons.mind: Depends on the drug or toxin.
eclipse-phase.rule.coated-weapons.who_may: A character with a coated melee weapon.
eclipse-phase.rule.coated-weapons.where_from: Coatings may include substances from poison-gland ware.
eclipse-phase.rule.coated-weapons.combines: Only the next damaging hit delivers the dose.
eclipse-phase.rule.coated-weapons.blocked_reason: It is a single-use payload delivery rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.placing-explosives.name: Placing Explosives

effect.summary: Demolition tests can increase structural damage, shape a blast, target a weak point, or make a charge harder to disarm.

eclipse-phase.rule.placing-explosives.cost_or_limit: Each superior success adds damage against structures; shaping can double or triple damage depending on blast angle.
eclipse-phase.rule.placing-explosives.go_wrong: A deliberately difficult charge requires an opposed disarm test.
eclipse-phase.rule.placing-explosives.combines: Knowledge of engineering may assist as a complementary skill.
eclipse-phase.rule.placing-explosives.blocked_reason: Shaped blasts and structural effects require spatial and object-target rules.

eclipse-phase.rule.making-explosives.name: Making Explosives

effect.summary: A trained character can manufacture explosives from gathered or fabricated raw materials.

eclipse-phase.rule.making-explosives.cost_or_limit: A task takes one hour per 1d10 damage value.
eclipse-phase.rule.making-explosives.go_wrong: Failure wastes resources; superior failure creates an unexpectedly weak or strong charge; critical failure triggers an explosion.
eclipse-phase.rule.making-explosives.who_may: A character trained in demolition hardware.
eclipse-phase.rule.making-explosives.where_from: Materials can be gathered or nanofabricated.
eclipse-phase.rule.making-explosives.combines: Restricted nanofabbers can still supply mundane materials.
eclipse-phase.rule.making-explosives.blocked_reason: It is a crafting and failure rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.shock-attacks.name: Shock Attacks

effect.summary: Electrical attacks can incapacitate biological targets; synthmorphs, bots, and vehicles are immune.

eclipse-phase.rule.shock-attacks.cost_or_limit: Targets check SOM with armor and size modifiers; success stuns briefly, failure incapacitates longer.
eclipse-phase.rule.shock-attacks.go_wrong: Failure removes neuromuscular control and causes a fall.
eclipse-phase.rule.shock-attacks.who_may: Shock attacks affect biomorphs and other biological creatures.
eclipse-phase.rule.shock-attacks.combines: A touch can deliver shock without damage; a normal melee attack delivers shock and damage.
eclipse-phase.rule.shock-attacks.blocked_reason: It can be represented as a target check and condition.

eclipse-phase.rule.wielding-two-or-more-.name: Wielding Two or More Weapons

effect.summary: Additional melee weapons or limbs increase attack damage or defense; multiple ranged weapons can fire at one target with cumulative penalties.

eclipse-phase.rule.wielding-two-or-more-.cost_or_limit: Melee damage bonus caps at three added dice; ranged attacks take a cumulative penalty; each separate target needs its own action.
eclipse-phase.rule.wielding-two-or-more-.who_may: Characters with multiple weapons or limbs.
eclipse-phase.rule.wielding-two-or-more-.where_from: Extra limbs can come from a multi-limbed morph.
eclipse-phase.rule.wielding-two-or-more-.combines: Some paired claws or gloves count as pairs.
eclipse-phase.rule.wielding-two-or-more-.blocked_reason: It is resolved with ordinary attacks and modifiers.

eclipse-phase.rule.durability.name: Durability

effect.summary: Reaching Durability incapacitates a biomorph or disables and crashes a synthmorph mind-state.

eclipse-phase.rule.durability.cost_or_limit: Damage must be reduced below Durability before recovery from the resulting state.
eclipse-phase.rule.durability.go_wrong: Accumulated harm causes collapse or system failure.
eclipse-phase.rule.durability.combines: Damage may be reduced by medical care, repair, or natural healing.
eclipse-phase.rule.durability.blocked_reason: It is a damage threshold rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.wounds.name: Wounds

effect.summary: A single attack causes wounds when its armor-reduced damage reaches multiples of one-fifth Durability.

eclipse-phase.rule.wounds.cost_or_limit: Each wound penalizes tests and initiative; wounds can cause knockdown or unconsciousness.
eclipse-phase.rule.wounds.go_wrong: Multiple wounds at once can knock a target unconscious or take a synthmorph offline.
eclipse-phase.rule.wounds.combines: Some traits, ware, drugs, psi sleights, and pools can negate limited wound penalties.
eclipse-phase.rule.wounds.blocked_reason: It needs injury states and their associated penalties.

eclipse-phase.rule.bleeding-out.name: Bleeding Out

effect.summary: A wounded biomorph at or beyond Durability must stabilize or accumulate further damage each turn.

eclipse-phase.rule.bleeding-out.cost_or_limit: Healing spray or medication improves self-stabilization; medichines stabilize automatically and induce stasis.
eclipse-phase.rule.bleeding-out.go_wrong: Failure causes damage per wound each action turn until care or death.
eclipse-phase.rule.bleeding-out.who_may: Biomorphs with a wound and damage at least equal to Durability.
eclipse-phase.rule.bleeding-out.combines: Another character can attempt a paramedic test to stabilize the victim.
eclipse-phase.rule.bleeding-out.blocked_reason: It requires timed damage and stabilization states.

eclipse-phase.rule.death-rating.name: Death Rating

effect.summary: At the death threshold, a biomorph dies or a synthmorph is destroyed beyond repair.

eclipse-phase.rule.death-rating.cost_or_limit: Threshold is one and a half times Durability for biomorphs and twice Durability for synthmorphs.
eclipse-phase.rule.death-rating.go_wrong: The body dies or becomes irreparable.
eclipse-phase.rule.death-rating.combines: Retrievable cortical stacks or backups may allow return.

eclipse-phase.rule.death-and-resleeving.name: Death and Resleeving

effect.summary: A retrieved cortical stack can permit resurrection in a new morph; otherwise an archived backup can restore a character.

eclipse-phase.rule.death-and-resleeving.cost_or_limit: Recovery depends on backup insurance or someone willing to retrieve the stack or supply a backup.
eclipse-phase.rule.death-and-resleeving.go_wrong: Without a retrievable stack, backup, or alpha fork, the character is permanently dead.
eclipse-phase.rule.death-and-resleeving.mind: Ego can return through a retrieved stack or archived backup.
eclipse-phase.rule.death-and-resleeving.who_may: Characters with recoverable stacks or backups.
eclipse-phase.rule.death-and-resleeving.where_from: Cortical stacks, archives, or alpha forks.
eclipse-phase.rule.death-and-resleeving.combines: Requires resleeving into a new morph when restored from a stack.
eclipse-phase.rule.death-and-resleeving.blocked_reason: The basic effect grammar cannot represent backup persistence, restoration, or permanent death.

eclipse-phase.rule.first-aid.name: First Aid

effect.summary: Successful first aid removes one wound and damage; critical failure inflicts damage.

eclipse-phase.rule.first-aid.cost_or_limit: Requires a tool kit and a 10-minute task plus 10 minutes per wound; treatment must occur within 24 hours and each injury set can be treated only once.
eclipse-phase.rule.first-aid.combines: Cannot treat injuries already treated by first aid or specified medical treatments.
eclipse-phase.rule.first-aid.blocked_reason: The procedure is representable as removing damage and wounds with a stated failure cost.

eclipse-phase.rule.recovery.name: Recovery

effect.summary: Recovery rates depend on morph and available medical technology.

eclipse-phase.rule.recovery.cost_or_limit: Heal damage before wounds; only the fastest technological healing source applies, and poor or harsh conditions multiply recovery time.
eclipse-phase.rule.recovery.go_wrong: Poor conditions double healing time; harsh conditions triple it.
eclipse-phase.rule.recovery.combines: Technological healing can add to morph biomod healing but cannot combine with another technological source.
eclipse-phase.rule.recovery.blocked_reason: Recovery uses ordinary time-based vitality restoration.

eclipse-phase.rule.surgery.name: Surgery

effect.summary: Required surgery must succeed before damage or wounds can be healed.

eclipse-phase.rule.surgery.cost_or_limit: A Medicine: Biotech task, usually taking one to four hours.
eclipse-phase.rule.surgery.who_may: A trained transhuman or medical bot
eclipse-phase.rule.surgery.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward prerequisite to healing.

eclipse-phase.rule.regeneration.name: Regeneration

effect.summary: Biomods regrow severed body parts over time; healing vats speed the process.

eclipse-phase.rule.regeneration.cost_or_limit: An ear or finger takes a week and a limb takes a month without a vat.
eclipse-phase.rule.regeneration.blocked_reason: Regrowing missing anatomy requires form transformation.

eclipse-phase.rule.revivification.name: Revivification

effect.summary: A recently deceased biomorph can be revived after medical stasis and treatment.

eclipse-phase.rule.revivification.cost_or_limit: Stasis and revival must occur within 24 hours; revival takes an hour plus an hour per wound, or a vat takes a day.
eclipse-phase.rule.revivification.who_may: Recently deceased biomorphs treated by a medical specialist
eclipse-phase.rule.revivification.where_from: Medical kit and Medicine: Paramedic, or a healing vat
eclipse-phase.rule.revivification.combines: Treatment restores the character to one point below their Death Rating.
eclipse-phase.rule.revivification.blocked_reason: Revival assumes the person’s identity or ego remains recoverable after death.

eclipse-phase.rule.physical-repair.name: Physical Repair

effect.summary: A successful hardware task restores an object or synthmorph fully.

eclipse-phase.rule.physical-repair.cost_or_limit: Requires an appropriate Hardware field and a tool kit; takes one hour per five damage restored plus eight hours per wound.
eclipse-phase.rule.physical-repair.who_may: A character with the appropriate Hardware skill
eclipse-phase.rule.physical-repair.combines: Conditions and available tools modify the task.
eclipse-phase.rule.physical-repair.blocked_reason: The repair is a straightforward restoration of damage and wounds.

eclipse-phase.rule.stress-points.name: Stress points

effect.summary: Mental stress accumulates and may impair an ego when it reaches its limits.

eclipse-phase.rule.stress-points.cost_or_limit: Stress can be reduced by psychosurgery, long-term rest, or motivational recovery.
eclipse-phase.rule.stress-points.go_wrong: Accumulation can cause breakdown or permanent mental loss.
eclipse-phase.rule.stress-points.combines: Four categories are recognized; Hardening can confer immunity to specified categories.
eclipse-phase.rule.stress-points.blocked_reason: Stress is a measurable mental resource and threshold.

eclipse-phase.rule.lucidity-and-stress.name: Lucidity and Stress

effect.summary: Stress reaching Lucidity causes a breakdown and a mental disorder.

eclipse-phase.rule.lucidity-and-stress.cost_or_limit: Lucidity equals twice WIL; no more than one disorder can be acquired per month.
eclipse-phase.rule.lucidity-and-stress.go_wrong: Breakdown causes shock lasting 1d6 hours and a disorder.
eclipse-phase.rule.lucidity-and-stress.mind: Causes catatonia or dissociation and a disorder.
eclipse-phase.rule.lucidity-and-stress.who_may: Egos, including those in synthetic shells or infomorphs
eclipse-phase.rule.lucidity-and-stress.combines: A disorder can trigger again if stress is lowered and later reaches Lucidity.
eclipse-phase.rule.lucidity-and-stress.blocked_reason: The rule imposes a compelled mental state and disorder upon a threshold event.

eclipse-phase.rule.trauma.name: Trauma

effect.summary: Stress at or above the Trauma Threshold causes cumulative trauma penalties and possible stress responses.

eclipse-phase.rule.trauma.cost_or_limit: Multiple trauma effects stack; at most three trauma worth of modifiers can be negated.
eclipse-phase.rule.trauma.go_wrong: Failed checks may cause disorientation or an acute stress response.
eclipse-phase.rule.trauma.mind: May stun, compel behavior, or cause detachment.
eclipse-phase.rule.trauma.combines: Traits, ware, drugs, psi sleights, and pools may negate some modifiers.
eclipse-phase.rule.trauma.blocked_reason: Acute responses can compel attacks, flight, or nonresponse.

eclipse-phase.rule.insanity-rating.name: Insanity Rating

effect.summary: Stress reaching twice Lucidity permanently destroys the ego’s mind.

eclipse-phase.rule.insanity-rating.cost_or_limit: The threshold is Lucidity multiplied by two; recovery is impossible.
eclipse-phase.rule.insanity-rating.combines: No psych help or rest restores the mind.
eclipse-phase.rule.insanity-rating.blocked_reason: The rule defines irreversible loss of an ego’s mind-state.

eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery-care.name: Psychosurgery Care

effect.summary: Psychosurgery treats stress, trauma, and disorders in a required order.

eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery-care.cost_or_limit: At most one hour daily; stress must be healed before trauma, and trauma before disorders; treatment times are one, eight, and forty hours respectively.
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery-care.go_wrong: At GM discretion, critical failure can cause a disorder or other negative ego trait.
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery-care.mind: Treatment can alter neurological and behavioral patterns.
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery-care.who_may: A psychosurgery practitioner, including a muse with the skill
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery-care.combines: Traumas and disorders impose test penalties.
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery-care.blocked_reason: Treatment includes behavioral modification and neurological alteration.

eclipse-phase.rule.natural-healing.name: Natural Healing

effect.summary: Stress, trauma, or disorders can recover over time after successful checks.

eclipse-phase.rule.natural-healing.cost_or_limit: Requires periods without new stress or trauma: a month for stress or trauma, three months for a disorder.
eclipse-phase.rule.natural-healing.combines: Stress must be healed before trauma; disorders require a longer interval.
eclipse-phase.rule.natural-healing.blocked_reason: Recovery is represented as removal of mental damage over time.

eclipse-phase.rule.motivational-recovery.name: Motivational Recovery

effect.summary: Achieving a motivation-based goal can heal stress or, if stress-free, remove a trauma.

eclipse-phase.rule.motivational-recovery.cost_or_limit: Disorders cannot be healed this way.
eclipse-phase.rule.motivational-recovery.combines: Can grant a bonus to the next attempt to remove a disorder.
eclipse-phase.rule.motivational-recovery.blocked_reason: It removes a defined mental damage measure on a trigger.

eclipse-phase.rule.disorders.name: Disorders

effect.summary: A disorder activates when its trigger occurs and a WIL check fails.

eclipse-phase.rule.disorders.cost_or_limit: Treatment or buying off the negative trait can remove it.
eclipse-phase.rule.disorders.go_wrong: Episodes impair behavior and may prevent actions.
eclipse-phase.rule.disorders.mind: Affects actions and behavior during an episode.
eclipse-phase.rule.disorders.where_from: Character creation, exsurgent infection, or stress reaching Lucidity
eclipse-phase.rule.disorders.combines: Trauma also triggers disorders; others may assess or help end an episode.
eclipse-phase.rule.disorders.blocked_reason: Disorders can compel behavior and restrict what a character can do.

eclipse-phase.rule.hardening.name: Hardening

effect.summary: Repeated traumatic exposure can grant immunity to a category of stress.

eclipse-phase.rule.hardening.cost_or_limit: Five qualifying traumatic survivals are required; the unknown can never be hardened against.
eclipse-phase.rule.hardening.go_wrong: Hardening reduces WIL and Persuade tests by 10.
eclipse-phase.rule.hardening.mind: The character becomes detached and less empathetic.
eclipse-phase.rule.hardening.who_may: Characters without a related active disorder
eclipse-phase.rule.hardening.where_from: Repeated exposure to alienation, helplessness, or violence
eclipse-phase.rule.hardening.blocked_reason: The rule specifies a category immunity and its costs.

eclipse-phase.rule.smart-material-reshap.name: Smart-material reshaping

effect.summary: Nanomachines can change an object's shape, color, or texture; reshaping takes 1d6 minutes.

eclipse-phase.rule.smart-material-reshap.blocked_reason: The grammar does not model an item's nanomachines changing its state over time.

eclipse-phase.rule.microgravity-drift.name: Microgravity drift

effect.summary: Unanchored objects keep drifting in their last direction of motion.

eclipse-phase.rule.microgravity-drift.cost_or_limit: Objects eventually settle toward the densest part of a habitat or spacecraft.
eclipse-phase.rule.microgravity-drift.combines: Objects pushed or thrown travel straight until they hit something.
eclipse-phase.rule.microgravity-drift.blocked_reason: This can be represented as sustained movement.

eclipse-phase.rule.fire-behavior.name: Fire behavior

effect.summary: Fire damages burning things, may spread, and grows more damaging over time; it does not burn in vacuum.

eclipse-phase.rule.fire-behavior.cost_or_limit: In microgravity it grows more slowly and may extinguish without air circulation.
eclipse-phase.rule.fire-behavior.go_wrong: Damage rises every five turns, or every ten turns in microgravity, unless conditions or intervention reduce it.
eclipse-phase.rule.fire-behavior.combines: Rain and efforts to extinguish a blaze reduce its damage.
eclipse-phase.rule.fire-behavior.blocked_reason: The effect changes over an area and escalates over time.

eclipse-phase.rule.radiation-damage.name: Radiation damage

effect.summary: Ionizing radiation can damage biological life and neural networks, with severity depending on dose, exposure time, and shielding.

eclipse-phase.rule.radiation-damage.cost_or_limit: Shielding and nanomedicine can reduce harm but cannot stop every source.
eclipse-phase.rule.radiation-damage.go_wrong: Severe exposure can cause lasting impairment, unhealable damage, or death.
eclipse-phase.rule.radiation-damage.combines: Radiation also damages biological neural networks, causing flawed uploads and backups.
eclipse-phase.rule.radiation-damage.blocked_reason: Radiation can alter uploads and backups, a state of mind or identity not represented by the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.vacuum-survival.name: Vacuum survival

effect.summary: An unsealed biomorph can endure one minute in vacuum if curled up, eyes closed, and lungs emptied; asphyxiation follows afterward.

eclipse-phase.rule.vacuum-survival.cost_or_limit: Holding air or failing to use the survival posture doubles damage; inadequate thermal protection adds harm.
eclipse-phase.rule.vacuum-survival.go_wrong: Asphyxiation and cold exposure can cause impairment and death.
eclipse-phase.rule.vacuum-survival.who_may: Biomorphs without vacuum sealing are subject to the rule.
eclipse-phase.rule.vacuum-survival.combines: Asphyxiation rules govern the consequences after the first minute.
eclipse-phase.rule.vacuum-survival.blocked_reason: The stated delayed harm can be represented by the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.aptitude-improvement-.name: Aptitude improvement limit

effect.summary: Raising an aptitude costs one Rez Point per point, and aptitudes cannot exceed 30.

eclipse-phase.rule.aptitude-improvement-.cost_or_limit: One Rez Point per aptitude point; maximum 30.
eclipse-phase.rule.aptitude-improvement-.combines: Raising an aptitude also raises linked skills by the same amount, doubled for Fray and Perceive.

eclipse-phase.rule.skill-improvement-and.name: Skill improvement and expertise plateau

effect.summary: Skill advancement costs one Rez Point for five points, but skills at 60 or higher improve by at most one point per downtime week, and no skill exceeds 100.

eclipse-phase.rule.skill-improvement-and.cost_or_limit: Practice, study, or instruction; one point per week at 60+; maximum 100.
eclipse-phase.rule.skill-improvement-and.go_wrong: A roll of 99 remains a critical failure even at skill 100.
eclipse-phase.rule.skill-improvement-and.combines: New skills start from their linked aptitude.
eclipse-phase.rule.skill-improvement-and.blocked_reason: This rule can be represented as advancement limits.

eclipse-phase.rule.flex-pool-improvement.name: Flex pool improvement limit

effect.summary: Two Rez Points raise an ego's Flex pool by one, to a maximum of three.

eclipse-phase.rule.flex-pool-improvement.cost_or_limit: Two Rez Points per point; maximum pool of 3.
eclipse-phase.rule.flex-pool-improvement.who_may: Characters improving their ego Flex pool.

eclipse-phase.rule.rez-point-costs-for-d.name: Rez Point costs for downtime options

effect.summary: The listed options cost one Rez Point for five rep points, a specialization, a psi sleight, a language, or an aptitude point; a Flex point costs two.

eclipse-phase.rule.rez-point-costs-for-d.cost_or_limit: Costs are as listed; a skill specialization requires skill rating 30 and only one may be bought per skill.
eclipse-phase.rule.rez-point-costs-for-d.go_wrong: Some negative ego traits cannot be discarded; overcoming a trait may take weeks or months and costs Rez Points equal to its original CP bonus.
eclipse-phase.rule.rez-point-costs-for-d.combines: The passage also describes trait reduction and improvement as downtime activities.
eclipse-phase.rule.rez-point-costs-for-d.blocked_reason: These are costs and limits on character advancement.

eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-network-resilien.name: Mesh network resilience

effect.summary: Mesh devices relay data among themselves, routing around failed or cut-off nodes rather than relying on centralized infrastructure.

eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-network-resilien.go_wrong: A failed node can interrupt its own service, but traffic can seek another route.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-network-resilien.combines: Nodes act as ad-hoc servers and repeaters.

eclipse-phase.rule.privacy-mode.name: Privacy Mode

effect.summary: Hides a user's social profile and asks nearby sensors and devices not to track them.

eclipse-phase.rule.privacy-mode.cost_or_limit: Applies −30 to mesh tracking attempts; sensors or AIs may ignore the request, and some authorities can override it.
eclipse-phase.rule.privacy-mode.go_wrong: The request may be ignored; use may be considered rude in some situations.
eclipse-phase.rule.privacy-mode.combines: The authority override can be toggled off where permitted.
eclipse-phase.rule.privacy-mode.blocked_reason: Concealing profile information and affecting tracking fit the basic grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.puppeted-devices.name: Puppeted devices

effect.summary: Routes a device's access and traffic through a controller, which automatically accepts commands for it.

eclipse-phase.rule.puppeted-devices.cost_or_limit: Access to the device is subject to controller authentication and privileges.
eclipse-phase.rule.puppeted-devices.go_wrong: Compromising the controller can expose the puppeted device.
eclipse-phase.rule.puppeted-devices.who_may: Devices configured to use a controller.
eclipse-phase.rule.puppeted-devices.combines: PAN devices are puppeted through mesh inserts or an ecto; security components may be puppeted to a security node.
eclipse-phase.rule.puppeted-devices.blocked_reason: The rule describes a binding between network devices and command access.

eclipse-phase.rule.pan-access.name: PAN access

effect.summary: A user's mesh inserts or ecto control their personal devices, and others must pass through that hub to access them.

eclipse-phase.rule.pan-access.cost_or_limit: The user may share device access temporarily or permanently.
eclipse-phase.rule.pan-access.go_wrong: Anyone who hacks the user gains access to puppeted devices.
eclipse-phase.rule.pan-access.who_may: Users with a personal area network.
eclipse-phase.rule.pan-access.where_from: The user's mesh inserts or ecto.
eclipse-phase.rule.pan-access.combines: PAN devices are puppeted to the controller hub.
eclipse-phase.rule.pan-access.blocked_reason: The rule describes a controller-to-device access relationship.

eclipse-phase.rule.vpns.name: VPNs

effect.summary: Encrypted point-to-point tunnels link network nodes for private communications and resource sharing.

eclipse-phase.rule.vpns.cost_or_limit: A hacked node makes its traffic vulnerable; users can still be tracked, and VPN traffic is harder to sniff.
eclipse-phase.rule.vpns.go_wrong: A compromised node exposes traffic; sniffing a VPN requires an additional −30 modifier.
eclipse-phase.rule.vpns.where_from: Encrypted tunnels across the public mesh.
eclipse-phase.rule.vpns.combines: Used for mobile offices, social networks, tacnets, and multiplayer alternate-reality games.
eclipse-phase.rule.vpns.blocked_reason: The rule describes a secured connection between network nodes.

eclipse-phase.rule.tiered-systems.name: Tiered systems

effect.summary: Lower-tier nodes communicate only with recognized devices in the tier above, so access may require progressing through upper tiers.

eclipse-phase.rule.tiered-systems.cost_or_limit: Deeper tiers usually have stronger security; spoofing may sometimes defeat the arrangement.
eclipse-phase.rule.tiered-systems.who_may: Tiered networks such as hypercorp systems and habitats.
eclipse-phase.rule.tiered-systems.combines: Spoofing attacks can fake signals from a higher-tier node.
eclipse-phase.rule.tiered-systems.blocked_reason: This is a network access restriction.

eclipse-phase.rule.air-gapped-systems.name: Air-gapped systems

effect.summary: Physically separated systems cannot be accessed through the mesh; access requires physical connection or defeating their isolation.

eclipse-phase.rule.air-gapped-systems.cost_or_limit: Requires a physical connection, removal of radio blocking, or attachment of a transceiver.
eclipse-phase.rule.air-gapped-systems.who_may: Systems physically separated from the mesh.
eclipse-phase.rule.air-gapped-systems.where_from: Hardwiring, absent wireless transceivers, or radio-proof barriers.
eclipse-phase.rule.air-gapped-systems.combines: Used for high-security systems and psychosurgery servers.
eclipse-phase.rule.air-gapped-systems.blocked_reason: The restriction depends on physical access and isolation.

eclipse-phase.rule.interregional-communi.name: Interregional communication lag

effect.summary: Communications between distant habitats can take minutes or hours each way; task time includes transmission time for remote searches.

eclipse-phase.rule.interregional-communi.cost_or_limit: A 10-light-minute distance adds 20 minutes for a search sent out and its results returned; interruptions can increase delays.
eclipse-phase.rule.interregional-communi.go_wrong: Long-distance messages may be interfered with or bumped for higher-priority traffic.
eclipse-phase.rule.interregional-communi.who_may: Users communicating or acting across regions.
eclipse-phase.rule.interregional-communi.where_from: Finite light-speed transmission and distance between habitats.
eclipse-phase.rule.interregional-communi.combines: A transmitted search ALI or fork can search remotely; exoplanet access depends on gate openings.
eclipse-phase.rule.interregional-communi.blocked_reason: The rule adds delay to communication and task time.

eclipse-phase.rule.exoplanet-mesh-access.name: Exoplanet mesh access windows

effect.summary: Exoplanet meshes can be accessed only during brief openings of a pandora gate, with intervals that may last days, weeks, or months.

eclipse-phase.rule.exoplanet-mesh-access.cost_or_limit: Access depends on the gate's opening schedule.
eclipse-phase.rule.exoplanet-mesh-access.who_may: Users with access during a gate opening.

eclipse-phase.rule.ar-sensory-input.name: AR sensory input

effect.summary: Mesh data can be layered onto physical senses as images, text, sound, touch, taste, and smell, and can be customized or filtered.

eclipse-phase.rule.ar-sensory-input.cost_or_limit: AR input may be hacked or used as a vector for basilisk mind hacks.
eclipse-phase.rule.ar-sensory-input.go_wrong: Hacked input can be used against the user; intrusive adverts may distract or bypass blockers.
eclipse-phase.rule.ar-sensory-input.mind: Sensory data is experienced as apparently real, though often ghostly.
eclipse-phase.rule.ar-sensory-input.where_from: Public or authenticated AR channels and user-selected skins.
eclipse-phase.rule.ar-sensory-input.combines: Can overlay data on physical perception and be filtered or turned off.
eclipse-phase.rule.ar-sensory-input.blocked_reason: Presenting sensory information and filtering it fit the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.backup-and-fork-stora.name: Backup and fork storage

effect.summary: Inactive backups, forks, and egos are files that can be stored on any device, while activated infomorphs require a host or server.

eclipse-phase.rule.backup-and-fork-stora.cost_or_limit: Running an activated infomorph requires suitable hardware.
eclipse-phase.rule.backup-and-fork-stora.mind: Backups and forks are stored mind emulations.
eclipse-phase.rule.backup-and-fork-stora.who_may: People with backups, forks, or egos.
eclipse-phase.rule.backup-and-fork-stora.where_from: Body banks, a cyberbrain, or an ego bridge.
eclipse-phase.rule.backup-and-fork-stora.combines: Cyberbrains and ego bridges allow backups or forks to be made; servers and hosts run activated infomorphs.
eclipse-phase.rule.backup-and-fork-stora.blocked_reason: Backing up, forking, and running mind emulations require mind-state and execution capabilities beyond the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.xp-recording.name: XP recording

effect.summary: Morphs with mesh inserts can record and transmit experiences, with the depth depending on which sensory and emotional tracks are retained.

eclipse-phase.rule.xp-recording.cost_or_limit: The fidelity depends on the tracks kept; full XP includes exteroceptive, interoceptive, and emotive tracks.
eclipse-phase.rule.xp-recording.mind: Emotive and bodily experience may be included in the recording.
eclipse-phase.rule.xp-recording.combines: Can be shared with friends, networks, or the public.
eclipse-phase.rule.xp-recording.blocked_reason: Reproducing a person's subjective experience and its tracks needs capabilities beyond the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.entoptic-tags.name: Entoptic tags

effect.summary: Stores virtual data on a person, place, or object; tags move with the item and can be viewed in AR.

eclipse-phase.rule.entoptic-tags.cost_or_limit: Hidden tags may require a difficult Interface Test or access to suitable networks or devices; found tags may need decryption.
eclipse-phase.rule.entoptic-tags.go_wrong: Tags may be hidden or encrypted.
eclipse-phase.rule.entoptic-tags.who_may: People able to create or access the tag network.
eclipse-phase.rule.entoptic-tags.where_from: Networks local to the tagged item.
eclipse-phase.rule.entoptic-tags.combines: Tags can be linked to social networks or circles.
eclipse-phase.rule.entoptic-tags.blocked_reason: The rule attaches and retrieves information associated with a marked target.

eclipse-phase.rule.overloaded-devices.name: Overloaded devices

effect.summary: A strained device imposes a −10 to −30 modifier on mesh actions involving it, prevents Insight use for those tests, and doubles the chance of a mesh-combat glitch.

eclipse-phase.rule.overloaded-devices.cost_or_limit: Can result from intensive processes, attacks, outages, crisis traffic, solar flares, or similar strain.
eclipse-phase.rule.overloaded-devices.go_wrong: Device performance is impaired and mesh-combat glitch risk rises.
eclipse-phase.rule.overloaded-devices.who_may: Mesh users acting through an overloaded device.
eclipse-phase.rule.overloaded-devices.combines: May affect hosts, servers, or other devices.
eclipse-phase.rule.overloaded-devices.blocked_reason: This is a mechanical penalty and glitch-risk rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.service-connection-an.name: Service connection and logging

effect.summary: A service works only while directly connected to its provider; services may log a user's mesh ID and enable tracking.

eclipse-phase.rule.service-connection-an.cost_or_limit: Jamming, distance lag, or other disconnection can remove access.
eclipse-phase.rule.service-connection-an.go_wrong: Service logs may expose user activity and identity.
eclipse-phase.rule.service-connection-an.where_from: Cloud software running on mesh servers.
eclipse-phase.rule.service-connection-an.combines: Services may offer search, translation, decryption, games, or other functions.
eclipse-phase.rule.service-connection-an.blocked_reason: This is a connection restriction and logging rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.stealthed-wireless-si.name: Stealthed wireless signals

effect.summary: Spread-spectrum, frequency-hopping, and modulation techniques make radio signals harder to detect.

eclipse-phase.rule.stealthed-wireless-si.cost_or_limit: Detection requires a complex opposed Interface Test, with the scanner at −30; short-burst signals can only be detected while transmitting.
eclipse-phase.rule.stealthed-wireless-si.go_wrong: A dedicated monitor may identify otherwise silent operatives by correlating surveillance and mesh signals.
eclipse-phase.rule.stealthed-wireless-si.who_may: Devices configured to stealth their radio signals.
eclipse-phase.rule.stealthed-wireless-si.combines: Covert operatives may use a separate PAN to distract from a stealthed one.
eclipse-phase.rule.stealthed-wireless-si.blocked_reason: Concealing and detecting signals fit the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.vpn-sniffing-duration.name: VPN sniffing duration

effect.summary: A successful VPN sniff lasts 1d6 minutes before another −30 Hacking Test is required because VPN keys change.

eclipse-phase.rule.vpn-sniffing-duration.cost_or_limit: Superior successes can extend the duration by 1d6 minutes or make detection harder.
eclipse-phase.rule.vpn-sniffing-duration.go_wrong: The defender may detect the interception and take countermeasures.
eclipse-phase.rule.vpn-sniffing-duration.combines: VPNs monitor latency and related clues for sniffing.
eclipse-phase.rule.vpn-sniffing-duration.blocked_reason: The rule limits the duration of intercepted information.

eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-encrypted-com.name: Quantum-encrypted communications

effect.summary: Quantum-encrypted communications cannot be sniffed.

eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-encrypted-com.combines: Distinguished from ordinary wireless and VPN traffic.
eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-encrypted-com.blocked_reason: It specifies an absolute restriction on information interception.

eclipse-phase.rule.laser-links-cannot-be.name: Laser links cannot be sniffed

effect.summary: Laser-link communications cannot be sniffed.

eclipse-phase.rule.laser-links-cannot-be.cost_or_limit: Fog, smoke, dust, or other atmospheric contaminants can disrupt the link.
eclipse-phase.rule.laser-links-cannot-be.combines: Laser links are commonly used between nearby habitats.
eclipse-phase.rule.laser-links-cannot-be.blocked_reason: The rule combines a communications restriction with environmental disruption.

eclipse-phase.rule.simultaneous-system-a.name: Simultaneous system access

effect.summary: A user can connect to many systems but focus on one at a time; quick actions can address multiple systems, while a complex action targets only one.

eclipse-phase.rule.simultaneous-system-a.cost_or_limit: Complex actions affect one system at a time.
eclipse-phase.rule.simultaneous-system-a.combines: Commands may be sent to multiple meshed or puppeted devices with one quick action.
eclipse-phase.rule.simultaneous-system-a.blocked_reason: This is a procedure rule rather than a world mechanism.

eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-id-logging.name: Mesh ID logging

effect.summary: A unique mesh ID is generated on connection, used for most interactions, and logged to create a trace of activity.

eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-id-logging.cost_or_limit: Anonymizing services can help conceal a user's trail.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-id-logging.go_wrong: Logged activity can be used to track users; registered IDs may reveal identity and address.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-id-logging.where_from: The user's cranial computer or ecto.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-id-logging.combines: IDs associate with accounts and screen names.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-id-logging.blocked_reason: The rule records and exposes information associated with a user.

eclipse-phase.rule.account-access-privil.name: Account access privileges

effect.summary: Accounts determine what a user can see and do on a device or service.

eclipse-phase.rule.account-access-privil.cost_or_limit: Privileges depend on account type and system rules.
eclipse-phase.rule.account-access-privil.go_wrong: A compromised account shell may be attacked.
eclipse-phase.rule.account-access-privil.who_may: Users with accounts on mesh systems.
eclipse-phase.rule.account-access-privil.where_from: The system's account and access controls.
eclipse-phase.rule.account-access-privil.combines: The four types are public, user, security, and admin.
eclipse-phase.rule.account-access-privil.blocked_reason: This is a system access restriction.

eclipse-phase.rule.public-accounts.name: Public Accounts

effect.summary: Allows anyone on the mesh to view and download public data, and sometimes to write to public areas.

eclipse-phase.rule.public-accounts.cost_or_limit: Usually offers little beyond public-data access.
eclipse-phase.rule.public-accounts.combines: Requires no authentication beyond the mesh ID.
eclipse-phase.rule.public-accounts.blocked_reason: The rule defines the scope of public access.

eclipse-phase.rule.user-accounts.name: User Accounts

effect.summary: Lets regular users use standard features and manage their own or shared data.

eclipse-phase.rule.user-accounts.cost_or_limit: Users generally cannot create accounts, access logs, alter security, or disrupt system functions.
eclipse-phase.rule.user-accounts.who_may: Employees, clients, and other regular system users.
eclipse-phase.rule.user-accounts.blocked_reason: The rule defines access privileges and restrictions.

eclipse-phase.rule.security-accounts.name: Security Accounts

effect.summary: Allows security users to inspect and edit logs, command security features, and manage ordinary accounts and user data.

eclipse-phase.rule.security-accounts.cost_or_limit: Requires authentication and has fewer privileges than admin access.
eclipse-phase.rule.security-accounts.who_may: Security personnel and ALIs monitoring a system.
eclipse-phase.rule.security-accounts.combines: Includes more privileges than a standard user account.

eclipse-phase.rule.admin-accounts.name: Admin Accounts

effect.summary: Provides root control to alter system data and privileges, manage software, and shut down or reboot the system.

eclipse-phase.rule.admin-accounts.cost_or_limit: Each system has one root admin account that cannot be deleted or lose its privileges.
eclipse-phase.rule.admin-accounts.blocked_reason: The rule defines privileged access and an invariant root account.

eclipse-phase.rule.biometric-scan.name: Biometric Scan

effect.summary: Authenticates a user by scanning one or more bodily signatures such as fingerprints, retinal patterns, or DNA.

eclipse-phase.rule.biometric-scan.cost_or_limit: Impractical for synthmorphs and frequent resleeving.
eclipse-phase.rule.biometric-scan.combines: May be one of several authentication methods required by a secure system.
eclipse-phase.rule.biometric-scan.blocked_reason: The mechanism senses biometric information to verify identity.

eclipse-phase.rule.ego-scan.name: Ego Scan

effect.summary: Authenticates a user's ego ID through a brainwave scan.

eclipse-phase.rule.ego-scan.cost_or_limit: Requires a hardwired, tamper-proof brainprint scanner and is generally used in high-security sites.
eclipse-phase.rule.ego-scan.who_may: Users with a scannable ego and access to the scanner.
eclipse-phase.rule.ego-scan.combines: May be combined with other authentication methods.
eclipse-phase.rule.ego-scan.blocked_reason: Verifying ego identity through a brain scan requires mind-state recognition beyond the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.direct-neural-interfa.name: Direct Neural Interface

effect.summary: Uses physical nervous-system connections to authenticate an implanted user.

eclipse-phase.rule.direct-neural-interfa.cost_or_limit: Requires implants or embedded hardware directly spliced into the nervous system.
eclipse-phase.rule.direct-neural-interfa.who_may: Users with linked implants or embedded hardware.
eclipse-phase.rule.direct-neural-interfa.combines: May be one of several authentication methods.
eclipse-phase.rule.direct-neural-interfa.blocked_reason: The rule uses a physical connection to establish access.

eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-id-authenticatio.name: Mesh ID authentication

effect.summary: Uses a user's mesh ID as proof of identity for systems that accept it.

eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-id-authenticatio.cost_or_limit: Common for public systems; systems accepting only specific IDs are vulnerable to spoofing.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-id-authenticatio.who_may: Users with a mesh ID accepted by the system.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-id-authenticatio.combines: Mesh IDs are otherwise used to log online interactions.

eclipse-phase.rule.other-account-authent.name: Other Account authentication

effect.summary: An active account on one system can grant access to related systems or services.

eclipse-phase.rule.other-account-authent.cost_or_limit: Applies only where systems provide linked access.
eclipse-phase.rule.other-account-authent.go_wrong: Compromising a controller account may grant access to its puppeted devices.
eclipse-phase.rule.other-account-authent.who_may: Users logged into a qualifying related account.
eclipse-phase.rule.other-account-authent.where_from: Linked system accounts or a controller device.
eclipse-phase.rule.other-account-authent.combines: Used for related services and puppeted devices.
eclipse-phase.rule.other-account-authent.blocked_reason: The rule grants access based on an existing relationship.

eclipse-phase.rule.passcode.name: Passcode

effect.summary: Grants access to an account to anyone who supplies its passcode.

eclipse-phase.rule.passcode.cost_or_limit: Passcodes are usually long and stored encrypted in mesh inserts.
eclipse-phase.rule.passcode.go_wrong: Anyone who obtains the passcode can access the account.
eclipse-phase.rule.passcode.who_may: Anyone able to provide the correct passcode.
eclipse-phase.rule.passcode.combines: May be one of multiple methods required by secure systems.
eclipse-phase.rule.passcode.blocked_reason: The mechanism checks a supplied secret.

eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-encrypted-com.name: Quantum-encrypted communications resist interception

effect.summary: Quantum communications detect external interference, so interception attempts fail.

eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-encrypted-com.cost_or_limit: Applies to communication channels, not basic file encryption; requires previously entangled devices.
eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-encrypted-com.blocked_reason: This is a communications security rule, not a character power.

eclipse-phase.rule.public-key-encryption.name: Public-key encryption resists ordinary codebreaking

effect.summary: Public-key-encrypted files are effectively unbreakable without a quantum computer.

eclipse-phase.rule.public-key-encryption.cost_or_limit: A quantum computer can break the encryption over a week-long task.
eclipse-phase.rule.public-key-encryption.blocked_reason: This rule defines how encryption strength works in the setting.

eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-key-setup.name: Quantum-key setup

effect.summary: Communications devices must be entangled together in the same place before being separated for secure communication.

eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-key-setup.cost_or_limit: Setup is costly and becomes less practical over long distances.
eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-key-setup.blocked_reason: This is a setup and logistics rule for secure communications.

eclipse-phase.rule.deleted-files-can-be-.name: Deleted files can be recovered

effect.summary: A deleted file remains recoverable for a limited period unless it is wiped.

eclipse-phase.rule.deleted-files-can-be-.cost_or_limit: Recovery requires an Interface Test and is possible for one week; archived backups may also exist.
eclipse-phase.rule.deleted-files-can-be-.who_may: A person with the means to make the test.
eclipse-phase.rule.deleted-files-can-be-.combines: Secure wiping prevents ordinary recovery, but backups may persist.
eclipse-phase.rule.deleted-files-can-be-.blocked_reason: This is a rule governing persistence and recovery of data.

eclipse-phase.rule.wiping-a-system.name: Wiping a system

effect.summary: A system wipe erases the system's data, software, accounts, infomorphs, and operating system.

eclipse-phase.rule.wiping-a-system.cost_or_limit: Takes one minute for motes, three minutes for hosts, and ten minutes for servers; secure wiping doubles the time.
eclipse-phase.rule.wiping-a-system.go_wrong: Forensic recovery may work until the system is reinstalled unless it was securely wiped.
eclipse-phase.rule.wiping-a-system.combines: Infomorphs receive warning and can copy themselves or move before the wipe completes.
eclipse-phase.rule.wiping-a-system.blocked_reason: The rule can erase active digital minds and therefore needs to represent their state and survival.

eclipse-phase.rule.script-step-limit.name: Script step limit

effect.summary: A script cannot contain more steps than the programmer's Program skill divided by ten.

eclipse-phase.rule.script-step-limit.cost_or_limit: The number of steps is limited by Program skill.
eclipse-phase.rule.script-step-limit.blocked_reason: This is a direct limit on a game mechanism.

eclipse-phase.rule.scripts-inherit-accou.name: Scripts inherit account privileges

effect.summary: A running script has the privileges of the account that runs it.

eclipse-phase.rule.scripts-inherit-accou.cost_or_limit: Tests use the programmer's Infosec, Interface, and Research skills, but only the script's Insight pools.
eclipse-phase.rule.scripts-inherit-accou.who_may: A script loaded by a user with the necessary access.
eclipse-phase.rule.scripts-inherit-accou.blocked_reason: This is a rule for how scripted actions inherit authority.

eclipse-phase.rule.home-device-destructi.name: Home-device destruction and shutdown

effect.summary: A shutdown home device stops its infomorph, while destruction kills it unless data can be recovered.

eclipse-phase.rule.home-device-destructi.cost_or_limit: Data may be recoverable from salvaged components, possibly resulting in a vapor.
eclipse-phase.rule.home-device-destructi.combines: The infomorph reboots along with a device that is merely shut down.
eclipse-phase.rule.home-device-destructi.blocked_reason: This rule determines how digital minds persist through shutdown and destruction.

eclipse-phase.rule.distributed-infomorph.name: Distributed Infomorphs

effect.summary: An infomorph can distribute its processing and storage across multiple devices.

eclipse-phase.rule.distributed-infomorph.cost_or_limit: A mote-only distribution needs at least five motes; fewer incurs overloaded-device penalties, and more than ten devices adds communication-lag penalties.
eclipse-phase.rule.distributed-infomorph.go_wrong: A crash on any participating device causes a wound; wider distribution increases hacking exposure.
eclipse-phase.rule.distributed-infomorph.mind: Communication lag can impair the distributed mind.
eclipse-phase.rule.distributed-infomorph.who_may: Infomorphs with access to multiple devices.
eclipse-phase.rule.distributed-infomorph.combines: Makes tracking harder and requires crashing each device to fully defeat the infomorph; re-integration takes time.
eclipse-phase.rule.distributed-infomorph.blocked_reason: A mind distributed across multiple simultaneous devices needs a multi-location storage and state model.

eclipse-phase.rule.moving-between-device.name: Moving between devices

effect.summary: An infomorph copies itself to an accessible device, activates there, and erases itself from the old device.

eclipse-phase.rule.moving-between-device.cost_or_limit: Takes one full action turn, during which the infomorph cannot act; it runs on only one home device at a time.
eclipse-phase.rule.moving-between-device.go_wrong: Ongoing actions may be suspended or disrupted during the move.
eclipse-phase.rule.moving-between-device.mind: Continuity is preserved and the process is not resleeving.
eclipse-phase.rule.moving-between-device.who_may: An infomorph with access to the destination.
eclipse-phase.rule.moving-between-device.combines: Egocasting is a long-distance version with a longer timeframe.
eclipse-phase.rule.moving-between-device.blocked_reason: Moving a running mind between devices while preserving continuity requires transfer of an active state.

eclipse-phase.rule.copying-an-infomorph.name: Copying an infomorph

effect.summary: An infomorph can create an alpha fork of itself.

eclipse-phase.rule.copying-an-infomorph.cost_or_limit: Takes one full action turn; commercial infomorph code normally prevents multiple running copies.
eclipse-phase.rule.copying-an-infomorph.go_wrong: Copying may be illegal; jurisdictions may require copylock and auto-erase meshware.
eclipse-phase.rule.copying-an-infomorph.mind: Copies retain continuity and include a signed copy number.
eclipse-phase.rule.copying-an-infomorph.who_may: An infomorph able to perform the copy.
eclipse-phase.rule.copying-an-infomorph.combines: Copying into another infomorph type counts as resleeving.
eclipse-phase.rule.copying-an-infomorph.blocked_reason: Forking creates multiple continuing versions of a mind and requires an identity-state rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.deleting-an-infomorph.name: Deleting an infomorph

effect.summary: An infomorph can delete itself unless it lacks privileges or is imprisoned.

eclipse-phase.rule.deleting-an-infomorph.go_wrong: Deletion may be unavailable without the necessary privileges or while confined.
eclipse-phase.rule.deleting-an-infomorph.who_may: An infomorph with sufficient privileges and freedom.
eclipse-phase.rule.deleting-an-infomorph.blocked_reason: The rule governs the ending of an active digital mind.

eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-backups.name: Infomorph backups

effect.summary: Infomorph memory and code changes are automatically written to backup files.

eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-backups.cost_or_limit: Regular secure backups are arranged away from the home device.
eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-backups.go_wrong: A deactivated infomorph remembers only up to shutdown; the passage does not specify other failure effects.
eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-backups.mind: Preserves memories and code up to the backup point.
eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-backups.where_from: Automatic writes to ego files and separately arranged secure sites.
eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-backups.combines: Infomorphs do not use cortical stacks.
eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-backups.blocked_reason: Persistent backups define which version of a digital mind can survive.

eclipse-phase.rule.search-misinformation.name: Search misinformation

effect.summary: Incorrect, outdated, and deliberately seeded false information can persist and spread through mesh searches.

eclipse-phase.rule.search-misinformation.cost_or_limit: Reputation ranking and crowdsourced verification can help counter misinformation.
eclipse-phase.rule.search-misinformation.go_wrong: Searches may return false or misleading information.
eclipse-phase.rule.search-misinformation.where_from: Errors, memetic warfare, and deliberate data seeding.
eclipse-phase.rule.search-misinformation.blocked_reason: This is a setting rule about the reliability of online information.

eclipse-phase.rule.research-critical-fai.name: Research critical failure

effect.summary: A critical failure on a Research Test produces false and misleading information.

eclipse-phase.rule.research-critical-fai.blocked_reason: This is a procedure-linked rule about information obtained through research.

eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-activity-traces.name: Mesh activity traces

effect.summary: System interactions leave recorded traces, often including identifying and usage data.

eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-activity-traces.cost_or_limit: The amount and type of recorded data vary by system and service.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-activity-traces.go_wrong: Records may expose a user’s identity, habits, or connections.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-activity-traces.who_may: Applies to users interacting with mesh systems
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-activity-traces.combines: Data may be shared with vendors, brokers, or advertising networks.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-activity-traces.blocked_reason: The rule is a basic information-adding effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-positioning-accu.name: Mesh positioning accuracy

effect.summary: Mesh positioning locates a target to within about five metres and can monitor movement while wireless connection continues.

eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-positioning-accu.cost_or_limit: The target must maintain an active wireless connection for ongoing monitoring.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-positioning-accu.who_may: Users with access to local directory location data
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-positioning-accu.combines: Location lookup requires knowing the target’s identity.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-positioning-accu.blocked_reason: The stated sensing and tracking effects fit the basic grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.anonymizing-service-t.name: Anonymizing-service trace limit

effect.summary: A trace of a user employing an anonymizing service reaches only that service.

eclipse-phase.rule.anonymizing-service-t.cost_or_limit: The service itself is the trace endpoint.
eclipse-phase.rule.anonymizing-service-t.who_may: Applies to users tracked through an anonymizing service
eclipse-phase.rule.anonymizing-service-t.combines: The Anonymizer is given as an example.
eclipse-phase.rule.anonymizing-service-t.blocked_reason: The rule describes a basic information-blocking effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.burner-mesh-id-trail.name: Burner mesh ID trail

effect.summary: The traceable trail ends when a burner ID stops being used, but it offers no protection during active use.

eclipse-phase.rule.burner-mesh-id-trail.cost_or_limit: Careless association with accounts or other data can reveal the user.
eclipse-phase.rule.burner-mesh-id-trail.go_wrong: A resourceful tracker may correlate its use with surveillance footage or other logs.
eclipse-phase.rule.burner-mesh-id-trail.combines: IDs may be used simultaneously, though correlation creates risk.
eclipse-phase.rule.burner-mesh-id-trail.blocked_reason: The rule’s effect is a basic conditional end to trace information.

eclipse-phase.rule.anonymous-account-log.name: Anonymous account logging

effect.summary: Interactions with an anonymous proxy account are not logged by the anonymizing service.

eclipse-phase.rule.anonymous-account-log.cost_or_limit: The account hides activity behind the service’s mesh ID.
eclipse-phase.rule.anonymous-account-log.combines: Multiple one-time accounts may be used.
eclipse-phase.rule.anonymous-account-log.blocked_reason: The rule is a basic removal of stored information.

eclipse-phase.rule.firewall-threat-model.name: Firewall threat modelling

effect.summary: Firewalls compare activity with learned patterns and may flag anomalies as intrusion.

eclipse-phase.rule.firewall-threat-model.cost_or_limit: Unusual location, timing, or activity may trigger scrutiny even when credentials are valid.
eclipse-phase.rule.firewall-threat-model.go_wrong: A mistaken anomaly judgement may downgrade an intruder’s status and trigger an alert.
eclipse-phase.rule.firewall-threat-model.blocked_reason: The rule is a basic information-sensing effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.firewall-rating-defen.name: Firewall rating defense

effect.summary: A firewall rating opposes hacking, unless the firewall is unavailable or active defense substitutes a defender’s skill.

eclipse-phase.rule.firewall-rating-defen.cost_or_limit: A deleted or crashed firewall leaves hacking unopposed unless active monitoring intervenes.
eclipse-phase.rule.firewall-rating-defen.combines: A system defender can actively take over firewall defense.
eclipse-phase.rule.firewall-rating-defen.blocked_reason: The rule is a basic conditional blocking effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-damage-and-crash.name: Mesh damage and crash

effect.summary: Software reaching its durability crashes, stopping transfers and processes; reaching death rating permanently corrupts it.

eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-damage-and-crash.cost_or_limit: Damage must meet or exceed durability or death rating, respectively.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-damage-and-crash.go_wrong: A crash can disconnect users, halt processes, or freeze a morph whose cyberbrain fails.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-damage-and-crash.mind: An infomorph or ego in a cyberbrain is effectively dead if its software is permanently corrupted.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-damage-and-crash.who_may: Applies to software, services, systems, cyberbrains, and infomorphs
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-damage-and-crash.combines: Crashes may be followed by automatic reboot for specified software and systems.
eclipse-phase.rule.mesh-damage-and-crash.blocked_reason: Permanent death of infomorphs and egos requires modeling mind-state and death beyond the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.automatic-software-re.name: Automatic software reboot

effect.summary: Infomorphs, cyberbrains, services, and operating systems reboot after crashing, clearing accumulated mesh damage and wounds.

eclipse-phase.rule.automatic-software-re.cost_or_limit: Rebooting takes one to six action turns.
eclipse-phase.rule.automatic-software-re.who_may: Applies to infomorphs, cyberbrains, services, and operating systems
eclipse-phase.rule.automatic-software-re.combines: A crashed program may still be attacked before reboot.
eclipse-phase.rule.automatic-software-re.blocked_reason: The stated delayed recovery and reset fit the basic grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.distributed-infomorph.name: Distributed infomorph durability

effect.summary: A distributed infomorph divides its durability evenly across devices, and a wound occurs if any device or its presence there crashes.

eclipse-phase.rule.distributed-infomorph.go_wrong: A single device crash can wound the distributed presence.
eclipse-phase.rule.distributed-infomorph.combines: Uses ordinary wound and crash rules.
eclipse-phase.rule.distributed-infomorph.blocked_reason: The stated allocation and crash condition can be represented with the basic grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.app-damage-repair.name: App damage repair

effect.summary: Rebooting an app removes its errors; damage and wounds are not repaired.

eclipse-phase.rule.app-damage-repair.cost_or_limit: Apps must be rebooted; damage is repaired before wounds.
eclipse-phase.rule.app-damage-repair.blocked_reason: The repair and reboot rule can be represented as a basic effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.redundancy-repair.name: Redundancy repair

effect.summary: Built-in redundancy repairs damage or wounds in infomorphs, cyberbrains, account shells, and operating systems.

eclipse-phase.rule.redundancy-repair.cost_or_limit: Repairs 1d10 damage or one wound per minute; damage is repaired first.
eclipse-phase.rule.redundancy-repair.blocked_reason: Automatic repair over time is representable in the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.device-glitch-chance.name: Device glitch chance

effect.summary: Physical device damage can cause a glitch; a wound causes one automatically.

eclipse-phase.rule.device-glitch-chance.cost_or_limit: Damage gives a 10% chance; a wound guarantees a glitch.
eclipse-phase.rule.device-glitch-chance.go_wrong: The glitch table determines the malfunction.
eclipse-phase.rule.device-glitch-chance.blocked_reason: A triggered malfunction can be represented by a basic effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.shock-disruption.name: Shock disruption

effect.summary: Shock prevents actions with or on the affected device for one action turn.

eclipse-phase.rule.shock-disruption.cost_or_limit: Lasts one action turn; the GM may also sever links or inflict damage.
eclipse-phase.rule.shock-disruption.go_wrong: May sever communications or cause extra damage.
eclipse-phase.rule.shock-disruption.combines: May affect implanted systems and infomorph riders.
eclipse-phase.rule.shock-disruption.blocked_reason: Temporary blocking of device use is supported by the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.destruction-rating-sh.name: Destruction Rating shutdown

effect.summary: A device stops functioning when damage exceeds its Destruction Rating.

eclipse-phase.rule.destruction-rating-sh.cost_or_limit: Damage must exceed the device’s Destruction Rating.
eclipse-phase.rule.destruction-rating-sh.go_wrong: Users lose their connection; resident infomorphs are effectively killed.
eclipse-phase.rule.destruction-rating-sh.combines: May end an infomorph’s operation if the device is its home.
eclipse-phase.rule.destruction-rating-sh.blocked_reason: The rule’s consequence for an infomorph’s death or continued existence involves digital ego states.

eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-rider-activ.name: Infomorph rider activity

effect.summary: An infomorph rider can remain active while its carrier rests, hibernates, or is incapacitated.

eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-rider-activ.cost_or_limit: Shock disrupts riders; damage thresholds can knock them offline or decommission them.
eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-rider-activ.go_wrong: A rider that survives damage at the Death Rating loses power after 48 hours.
eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-rider-activ.who_may: Infomorphs using ware in a morph as a home device
eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-rider-activ.where_from: A rider’s home device is carried by a morph
eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-rider-activ.combines: Muse or fork may ride in a carrier.
eclipse-phase.rule.infomorph-rider-activ.blocked_reason: Rider persistence and decommissioning require tracking a digital ego’s state and power dependency.

eclipse-phase.rule.glitches.name: Glitches

effect.summary: A glitch can drop links, reveal an intruder, erase access to memories or data, freeze software, or overload resources.

eclipse-phase.rule.glitches.cost_or_limit: A glitch result is determined by a 1d6 roll.
eclipse-phase.rule.glitches.go_wrong: Results range from lost connectivity to resource overload.
eclipse-phase.rule.glitches.mind: May block ego memories until reboot.
eclipse-phase.rule.glitches.where_from: Overload, hardware damage, or mesh combat
eclipse-phase.rule.glitches.combines: Includes cyberbrains, infomorphs, apps, firewalls, and operating systems.
eclipse-phase.rule.glitches.blocked_reason: The listed malfunctions can be modeled as changes to working, information, or memory.

eclipse-phase.rule.encoded-security.name: Encoded security

effect.summary: Hard-coded security makes attempts to hack cyberbrains and infomorphs more difficult.

eclipse-phase.rule.encoded-security.combines: Copylock apps add another modifier to copying.
eclipse-phase.rule.encoded-security.blocked_reason: A difficulty modifier is a standard game mechanic.

eclipse-phase.rule.terminate-cortical-st.name: Terminate Cortical Stack Feed

effect.summary: The data feed from a cyberbrain to a cortical stack, or from an infomorph to backup files, can be cut off.

eclipse-phase.rule.terminate-cortical-st.cost_or_limit: Can be temporary or indefinite; the cortical stack itself cannot be hacked through this connection.
eclipse-phase.rule.terminate-cortical-st.go_wrong: A restored backup lacks memories from the time the feed was cut.
eclipse-phase.rule.terminate-cortical-st.mind: Causes gaps in a restored ego’s memories.
eclipse-phase.rule.terminate-cortical-st.combines: Affects cortical stack feeds or infomorph backup updates.
eclipse-phase.rule.terminate-cortical-st.blocked_reason: The rule governs backup and restored ego states, not just ordinary information transfer.

eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-access.name: Simulspace access

effect.summary: A simulspace replaces the user’s sensorium with a virtual environment.

eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-access.cost_or_limit: Only servers may run simulspaces; access is via mesh, hardwire, or trode net.
eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-access.go_wrong: A crash or ejection returns control to the morph.
eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-access.mind: Experiences can have psychological impact despite being virtual.
eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-access.combines: Users select an avatar in a white room before entering.
eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-access.blocked_reason: The passage describes a broad virtual environment rather than one basic-grammar effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.domain-rules.name: Domain rules

effect.summary: Programmed rules may change physical forces, environment, healing, and transformation inside a simulspace.

eclipse-phase.rule.domain-rules.cost_or_limit: Admins can manipulate domain rules; deviations from real-time speed have limits.
eclipse-phase.rule.domain-rules.combines: Includes physics, environment, and time settings.
eclipse-phase.rule.domain-rules.blocked_reason: The rule can alter broad environmental laws across a virtual domain, beyond a basic targeted effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.time-distortion.name: Time distortion

effect.summary: A simulspace can run at a different rate from real time.

eclipse-phase.rule.time-distortion.cost_or_limit: Achieved speeds are up to 60 times faster or slower than real time.
eclipse-phase.rule.time-distortion.go_wrong: Meatspace conversations become extremely slow at accelerated rates.
eclipse-phase.rule.time-distortion.mind: The user experiences time at the simulation’s rate.
eclipse-phase.rule.time-distortion.combines: Does not change pool recharge rates.
eclipse-phase.rule.time-distortion.blocked_reason: Changing the flow of time relative to real time is outside the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-damage-and.name: Simulspace damage and death

effect.summary: Virtual injuries do not constitute physical harm; characters who die are usually ejected or moved to a white room.

eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-damage-and.cost_or_limit: Domain rules determine what happens to simulated deaths.
eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-damage-and.go_wrong: Mental stress or trauma carries over to the ego.
eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-damage-and.mind: Simulation trauma persists beyond the session.
eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-damage-and.combines: Vigor pool cannot be used in simulspace.
eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-damage-and.blocked_reason: The rule distinguishes simulated death from the ego’s ongoing state and carries mental consequences across the simulation.

eclipse-phase.rule.psi-restrictions-in-s.name: Psi restrictions in simulspace

effect.summary: Asyncs cannot use psi abilities in a simulspace, though effects may be simulated.

eclipse-phase.rule.psi-restrictions-in-s.cost_or_limit: Vigor pool is also unavailable; pool recharge remains at normal real-time rates.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-restrictions-in-s.combines: Time distortion does not change pool recharge.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-restrictions-in-s.blocked_reason: The rule explicitly prevents a class of powers from operating in the simulation.

eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-controls.name: Simulspace controls

effect.summary: Admins or authorized cheat users can control users, rules, items, privacy, travel, and sessions in a simulspace.

eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-controls.cost_or_limit: Some changes require Program or Hacking Tests; shutting down a large simulation takes time.
eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-controls.go_wrong: Unauthorized use may be detected and users may be evicted.
eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-controls.mind: Controls may dictate NPC responses or lock users in a session.
eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-controls.who_may: Admins and users with suitable cheat codes
eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-controls.combines: Includes teleportation, invisibility, invulnerability, and lockbox controls.
eclipse-phase.rule.simulspace-controls.blocked_reason: The described controls can affect whole domains and multiple users, beyond a basic targeted effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.psi-infection-and-per.name: Psi infection and persistence

effect.summary: Watts-MacLeod infection creates psi abilities that persist with the ego through uploading, forking, and resleeving.

eclipse-phase.rule.psi-infection-and-per.cost_or_limit: Psi requires a biological brain and nervous system to function.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-infection-and-per.go_wrong: Infection permanently fragments the async’s mind and grants an Addiction or Mental Disorder trait.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-infection-and-per.mind: Causes a permanent mental change and sub-strain compulsions.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-infection-and-per.combines: Psi abilities are ego-inherent, not morph traits.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-infection-and-per.blocked_reason: The infection and powers persist through copying and resleeving with the ego, a transfer rule beyond the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.psi-range-and-targets.name: Psi range and targets

effect.summary: Psi-chi affects only the async; psi-gamma works on biological life at short range, but not on machines, infomorphs, or simple life.

eclipse-phase.rule.psi-range-and-targets.cost_or_limit: Range and test modifiers vary by distance and target; thick barriers can block psi.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-range-and-targets.go_wrong: Psi against some creatures may be ineffective or penalized.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-range-and-targets.mind: Psi can affect biological minds and nervous systems.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-range-and-targets.combines: Asyncs and exsurgents are more susceptible to psi.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-range-and-targets.blocked_reason: Range and target restrictions can be represented as ordinary target limits.

eclipse-phase.rule.psi-opposed-tests.name: Psi opposed tests

effect.summary: A target resists a psi effect with a WIL Check opposed by the async’s Psi skill.
