eclipse-phase.rule.psi-opposed-tests.cost_or_limit: Both sides may spend Moxie; willing targets can forgo resistance if aware.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-opposed-tests.go_wrong: A critical failure inflicts 1d6 damage on the async; a critical defense locks the async out of that mind until recharge.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-opposed-tests.mind: Targets who succeed in their opposed test know an outside influence is acting.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-opposed-tests.combines: Critical successes increase potency; mental armor can reduce psychic damage.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-opposed-tests.blocked_reason: The rule includes direct influence on another mind and mental lockout.

eclipse-phase.rule.psi-duration.name: Psi duration

effect.summary: Psi sleights can be constant, instant, temporary, or sustained.

eclipse-phase.rule.psi-duration.cost_or_limit: Temporary duration depends on WIL; sustained use penalizes other tests and requires proximity.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-duration.go_wrong: Long sustained use may cause additional infection effects.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-duration.blocked_reason: The duration categories and concentration limits are directly representable.

eclipse-phase.rule.infection-modifiers.name: Infection modifiers

effect.summary: Psi-gamma use raises Infection Rating and triggers an Infection Test.

eclipse-phase.rule.infection-modifiers.cost_or_limit: Each sleight adds its Infection modifier; recharge lowers the rating.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-modifiers.go_wrong: The exovirus may gain a stronger hold over the async.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-modifiers.mind: May cause fatigue, headaches, bleeding, or psychological influence.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-modifiers.combines: Pushing a sleight also increases Infection Rating.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-modifiers.mechanism: power use cost and infection test
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-modifiers.blocked_reason: The escalating infection can alter the user’s mind and condition over time, beyond a simple fixed cost.

eclipse-phase.rule.infection-test.name: Infection Test

effect.summary: A successful test causes an influence effect; failure has no negative effect, and Moxie can avoid the test while Infection Rating still rises.

eclipse-phase.rule.infection-test.cost_or_limit: The target number is current Infection Rating including the sleight modifier; pool cannot be spent on the test.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-test.go_wrong: Critical failure grants immunity to influence until next recharge; critical success permits a delayed takeover or future test interference.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-test.mind: Successful tests let the exovirus exert more control over the psyche.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-test.who_may: Async using sleights that call for an Infection Test.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-test.combines: Superior successes increase the influence-effect roll.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-test.blocked_reason: The rule applies variable influence consequences and delayed infection complications.

eclipse-phase.rule.influence-effects.name: Influence effects

effect.summary: Successful Infection Tests trigger a sub-strain influence effect, with physical, behavioral, motivational, or other consequences.

eclipse-phase.rule.influence-effects.cost_or_limit: Effects begin immediately; behavior and motivation durations and severity depend on the effect and Infection Rating.
eclipse-phase.rule.influence-effects.go_wrong: May cause damage, behavioral restrictions, compulsions, frenzy, hallucinations, or stress.
eclipse-phase.rule.influence-effects.mind: May alter behavior, motivation, or perception.
eclipse-phase.rule.influence-effects.who_may: Infected asyncs after a successful Infection Test.
eclipse-phase.rule.influence-effects.combines: Superior successes modify the effect roll; influence effects must be satiated before Infection Rating can fall.
eclipse-phase.rule.influence-effects.blocked_reason: It produces a variable set of mental and physical consequences not expressible as one basic effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.pushing-sleights.name: Pushing sleights

effect.summary: A pushed sleight chooses one boost, such as increased range, effect, power, penetration, duration, or an extra target.

eclipse-phase.rule.pushing-sleights.cost_or_limit: Pushing psi-gamma doubles Infection Modifier and inflicts 1d6 damage before an Infection Test; pushing active psi-chi raises Infection Rating by 5 and tests; psi-chi pushes last WIL divided by 5 minutes.
eclipse-phase.rule.pushing-sleights.go_wrong: Increases infection influence and may cause physical damage.
eclipse-phase.rule.pushing-sleights.mind: Mental effort and pain may be apparent with a Kinesics Test.
eclipse-phase.rule.pushing-sleights.combines: Moxie can negate physical damage; spending 2 Moxie points negates the test entirely.
eclipse-phase.rule.pushing-sleights.blocked_reason: The rule modifies range, targets, duration, resistance, penetration, and the backlash of another power.

eclipse-phase.rule.infection-rating-thre.name: Infection Rating thresholds

effect.summary: At Rating 33 or higher psi-chi sleights gain Increased Effect; at 66 or higher psi-gamma sleights gain one shared free push effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.infection-rating-thre.cost_or_limit: Benefits cease when Rating drops below the corresponding threshold; an already provided push effect generally cannot be chosen again.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-rating-thre.who_may: Asyncs whose Infection Rating reaches the thresholds.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-rating-thre.combines: Threshold benefits interact with voluntary pushes; extra target is an exception to the duplicate-effect restriction.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-rating-thre.blocked_reason: It automatically modifies other powers based on a changing rating.

eclipse-phase.rule.easing-the-infection.name: Easing the Infection

effect.summary: Short recharge reduces Infection Rating by 10 and long recharge resets it to base, but active influence effects must first be satiated.

eclipse-phase.rule.easing-the-infection.cost_or_limit: Rating cannot drop below base, defined as Psi Level times 10.
eclipse-phase.rule.easing-the-infection.combines: Influence effects prevent reduction until satiated.
eclipse-phase.rule.easing-the-infection.blocked_reason: The rule changes a persistent infection state subject to a floor and a condition.

eclipse-phase.rule.psi-sleight-access-an.name: Psi sleight access and activation

effect.summary: Psi-chi sleights are passive and available to Psi characters; psi-gamma requires Psi Level 2 and active sleights use actions and Psi tests.

eclipse-phase.rule.psi-sleight-access-an.cost_or_limit: Unless specified otherwise, each sleight may be taken only once; gamma sleights may cause infection flare-ups.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-sleight-access-an.go_wrong: Gamma use may trigger infection consequences.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-sleight-access-an.mind: Psi-chi abilities are subconscious; gamma abilities require effort.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-sleight-access-an.who_may: Psi trait holders; Psi Level 2 is required for psi-gamma.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-sleight-access-an.combines: Targets that are sentient beings or life forms require opposed tests.
eclipse-phase.rule.psi-sleight-access-an.blocked_reason: These are access and test procedures rather than a world mechanism requiring an unavailable effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.backups-and-egos.name: Backups and egos

effect.summary: A backup records an ego's personality, memories, skills, and neural connections, allowing digital emulation, resleeving, infomorph operation, forking, or egocasting.

eclipse-phase.rule.backups-and-egos.cost_or_limit: A backup excludes the physical body; the book distinguishes stored backups from running egos by usage.
eclipse-phase.rule.backups-and-egos.mind: The stored record represents the transhuman ego.
eclipse-phase.rule.backups-and-egos.combines: Can be resleeved, run as an infomorph or fork, or egocast.
eclipse-phase.rule.backups-and-egos.blocked_reason: The rule concerns stored and running ego states, resleeving, forks, and transmission.

eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-backup.name: Cortical stack backup rate and contents

effect.summary: A stack records the ego once each second and also backs up mesh-insert data.

eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-backup.cost_or_limit: The passage gives a rate of 86,400 backups per Earth day; mesh data takes little space compared with the ego.
eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-backup.mind: The ego and neuronal connections are recorded.
eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-backup.who_may: Morphs equipped with cortical stacks and neural lace.
eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-backup.where_from: Cortical stack linked to a neural lace network or cyberbrain.
eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-backup.combines: Stores muse, lifelog, software, blueprints, and other accumulated data alongside the ego.
eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-backup.blocked_reason: It defines how an ego is preserved for later restoration.

eclipse-phase.rule.popping-a-stack.name: Popping a Stack

effect.summary: A cortical stack can be extracted from a morph; ideal surgery or workshop conditions make extraction automatic.

eclipse-phase.rule.popping-a-stack.cost_or_limit: Under poor conditions, requires a relevant Medicine or Hardware test; ordinary extraction takes four action turns, while taking the head takes two or one with a large blade.
eclipse-phase.rule.popping-a-stack.go_wrong: Removing a stack from an immobilized living morph inflicts 3d10+10 damage; victim, perpetrator, and witnesses risk 1d6 stress.
eclipse-phase.rule.popping-a-stack.who_may: A skilled extractor; test skill depends on morph type.
eclipse-phase.rule.popping-a-stack.where_from: The stack's implanted location, usually near the brain stem.
eclipse-phase.rule.popping-a-stack.combines: Biomorphs use Medicine: Paramedic; synthmorphs use Hardware: Robotics.
eclipse-phase.rule.popping-a-stack.blocked_reason: The stated extraction, damage, and test conditions can be handled as ordinary game procedures.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-cortical-stack-.name: Swarm cortical-stack recovery

effect.summary: Recovering a destroyed swarmanoid’s ego requires one-third of its mass and a six-hour Robotics task at a tools shop.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-cortical-stack-.cost_or_limit: At least one-third of the swarm’s mass, a tools shop, and six hours are required.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-cortical-stack-.blocked_reason: The procedure recovers and uploads an ego, a persistent identity state not represented by the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.transfer-and-fork-dis.name: Transfer and fork distinction

effect.summary: A transfer removes the source ego, while a fork copies it and leaves the original intact.

eclipse-phase.rule.transfer-and-fork-dis.blocked_reason: The rule distinguishes continuity and duplication of an ego, which the basic effect grammar cannot model.

eclipse-phase.rule.ego-bridge.name: Ego bridge

effect.summary: A bridge scans a biological brain and uses nanobots to reproduce its neural network in a destination morph.

eclipse-phase.rule.ego-bridge.cost_or_limit: Biological-brain transfer takes an hour; the subject remains conscious during the process.
eclipse-phase.rule.ego-bridge.mind: The subject remains awake during transfer.
eclipse-phase.rule.ego-bridge.combines: Used for biological-brain transfers and resleeving.
eclipse-phase.rule.ego-bridge.blocked_reason: The process reconstructs a neural network in another body and severs the original’s neural connections.

effect.summary: Uploading an ego normally requires no test.

eclipse-phase.rule.post-mortem-upload-wi.name: Post-mortem upload window

effect.summary: A dead biomorph’s ego can be recovered only if its brain tissue remains intact and death was within two hours.

eclipse-phase.rule.post-mortem-upload-wi.cost_or_limit: After death, each fifteen minutes costs five points from one chosen skill; a healing vat halts further loss but does not restore lost points.
eclipse-phase.rule.post-mortem-upload-wi.go_wrong: Skill loss accrues after death; damaged brain tissue makes recovery impossible.
eclipse-phase.rule.post-mortem-upload-wi.combines: A healing vat halts ongoing skill loss.
eclipse-phase.rule.post-mortem-upload-wi.blocked_reason: It governs whether an ego can be recovered from a corpse and how it degrades over time.

eclipse-phase.rule.backup-re-instancing.name: Backup re-instancing

effect.summary: A recovered stack or archived backup can be used to restore a person as an infomorph.

eclipse-phase.rule.backup-re-instancing.cost_or_limit: Re-instancing depends on recovery, available backup services, and the circumstances of death.
eclipse-phase.rule.backup-re-instancing.go_wrong: A stack may be lost, sold, destroyed, or held in storage; without a plan, death may be final.
eclipse-phase.rule.backup-re-instancing.mind: A restored ego may remember its death or suffer missing time and memories.
eclipse-phase.rule.backup-re-instancing.who_may: Backup services, local authorities, or polities may handle restoration.
eclipse-phase.rule.backup-re-instancing.where_from: A recovered cortical stack or archived backup.
eclipse-phase.rule.backup-re-instancing.combines: Basic backup insurance includes attempted retrieval and re-instancing.
eclipse-phase.rule.backup-re-instancing.blocked_reason: It models persistence and restoration of personal identity from stored ego states.

eclipse-phase.rule.basic-backup-insuranc.name: Basic Backup Insurance

effect.summary: Backup services attempt retrieval, restore a verified dead or long-missing client, and arrange an equivalent morph when available.

eclipse-phase.rule.basic-backup-insuranc.cost_or_limit: A missing-person waiting period is usually six months; repeated deaths during a short span can lower the available morph points.
eclipse-phase.rule.basic-backup-insuranc.go_wrong: Retrieval or restoration may fail if the stack or service cannot be found.
eclipse-phase.rule.basic-backup-insuranc.who_may: Characters with some form of backup insurance.
eclipse-phase.rule.basic-backup-insuranc.combines: May include hazardous retrieval or hardened storage as additional services.
eclipse-phase.rule.basic-backup-insuranc.blocked_reason: The rule governs ego backup, restoration, and continued identity after death.

eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-time.name: Resleeving time

effect.summary: Cyberbrain and infomorph resleeving takes one action turn; biological-brain resleeving takes an hour using an ego bridge.

eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-time.cost_or_limit: Biological-brain resleeving requires physical rewiring with an ego bridge.
eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-time.combines: Ego bridge is needed for biological-brain resleeving.
eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-time.blocked_reason: Resleeving moves an ego into a new body, a continuity operation outside basic effects.

eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-integratio.name: Resleeving integration

effect.summary: A new morph can cause temporary adjustment difficulties as the ego adapts to its body.

eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-integratio.cost_or_limit: A failed Integration Test imposes −10 to actions for one day, plus one day per superior failure.
eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-integratio.mind: Alienation and adjustment can be disorienting and may persist beyond physical acclimation.
eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-integratio.who_may: Characters taking on a new morph.
eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-integratio.combines: Exotic Morphology modifies the Integration Test.
eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-integratio.blocked_reason: The rule concerns adapting a mind to a changed body and its capabilities.

eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-snapsh.name: Cortical stack snapshot limit

effect.summary: A cortical stack holds only the latest saved ego snapshot, taken before trauma and cell-death cut-outs activate.

eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-snapsh.cost_or_limit: Iterative ego changes cannot be stored in the stack.
eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-snapsh.go_wrong: Restoration may include memories of the final moments before death.
eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-snapsh.mind: The restored person may experience fear and horror from remembered death.
eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-snapsh.who_may: People restored from a retrieved cortical stack.
eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-snapsh.combines: Counseling and psychosurgery can lessen the effects over time.
eclipse-phase.rule.cortical-stack-snapsh.blocked_reason: It defines the limits of stored ego state and memory across death.

eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-pool-trans.name: Resleeving pool transfer

effect.summary: A character gains the new morph’s pools, while points spent in the prior morph remain deducted until recharge.

eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-pool-trans.cost_or_limit: Previously spent pool points stay temporarily deducted.
eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-pool-trans.combines: Recharge action restores access to spent points.

eclipse-phase.rule.integration-test.name: Integration Test

effect.summary: A SOM Check determines how quickly a character acclimates to a new morph.

eclipse-phase.rule.integration-test.cost_or_limit: Only the ego’s Flex pool may be used on resleeving tests.
eclipse-phase.rule.integration-test.go_wrong: Failure applies −10 to actions for a day, plus one day per superior failure.
eclipse-phase.rule.integration-test.combines: The new morph’s Exotic Morphology modifier applies; Adaptability may help.

eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-stress-tes.name: Resleeving Stress Test

effect.summary: A WIL Check measures stress from alienation, discontinuity, remembered death, or lack.

eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-stress-tes.cost_or_limit: Only the ego’s Flex pool may be used on resleeving tests.
eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-stress-tes.go_wrong: Stress is inflicted according to the test’s stress value.
eclipse-phase.rule.resleeving-stress-tes.combines: Standard cases use SV 1d6; remembered death or lack over three months uses SV 1d10/1.

eclipse-phase.rule.morph-points.name: Morph Points

effect.summary: The GM assigns a budget of Morph Points for obtaining morphs and related options.

eclipse-phase.rule.morph-points.cost_or_limit: Six is the default; successive resleeves during a mission are recommended to lose one point each before boosts.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-points.where_from: GM-assigned mission resources and insurance abstraction.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-points.combines: Resources, rep favors, and negative morph traits may increase the budget.

eclipse-phase.rule.morph-availability-te.name: Morph Availability Test

effect.summary: A d100 roll against a morph’s Availability rating determines whether it is on hand.

eclipse-phase.rule.morph-availability-te.cost_or_limit: Local conditions and rep favors can modify availability; failed attempts require selecting another morph.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-availability-te.go_wrong: A failed test means that model is unavailable.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-availability-te.combines: Rep favors can improve the test if the applicable Rep Test succeeds.

eclipse-phase.rule.negative-morph-traits.name: Negative Morph Traits MP limit

effect.summary: Negative morph traits can grant extra Morph Points, up to six.

eclipse-phase.rule.negative-morph-traits.combines: Can be combined with Resources and rep favors.

eclipse-phase.rule.morph-modification.name: Morph modification

effect.summary: A morph can be customized using suitable skills, tools, and time.

eclipse-phase.rule.morph-modification.cost_or_limit: Biomorphs need a clinic or healing vat; synthmorphs need a Robotics shop; complexity determines a two-, eight-, or twenty-four-hour timeframe.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-modification.go_wrong: Untrustworthy or experimental services may produce unwanted or unreliable results.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-modification.who_may: Characters with appropriate skills and equipment, or service providers.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-modification.where_from: A clinic, healing vat, or Robotics shop.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-modification.combines: Ware must be acquired separately; restricted ware may need black-market service.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-modification.blocked_reason: It changes a morph’s physical form and may install ware.

eclipse-phase.rule.morph-fabrication.name: Morph fabrication

effect.summary: A morph can be fabricated or grown with blueprints or genetics, specialized facilities, and long skill-task timeframes.

eclipse-phase.rule.morph-fabrication.cost_or_limit: Needs suitable fabrication equipment and a medical facility; time cannot be reduced by accelerated VR.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-fabrication.go_wrong: Without source designs or genetics, creation takes much longer.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-fabrication.who_may: Characters with the required skills and access.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-fabrication.where_from: Nanofabricator or exowomb and medical facility.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-fabrication.combines: May use blueprints or genetics; fabrication is mostly automated.
eclipse-phase.rule.morph-fabrication.blocked_reason: It creates a physical body, which exceeds basic effect operations.

eclipse-phase.rule.acquiring-ware-with-a.name: Acquiring ware with a morph

effect.summary: Ware acquired alongside a morph is automatically installed in it.

eclipse-phase.rule.acquiring-ware-with-a.cost_or_limit: Ware still costs Morph Points or Gear Points as applicable.
eclipse-phase.rule.acquiring-ware-with-a.combines: Ware can be acquired with Morph Points or Gear Points.
eclipse-phase.rule.acquiring-ware-with-a.blocked_reason: It specifies that an acquired item becomes installed in a morph.

eclipse-phase.rule.repeat-resleeving-mp-.name: Repeat-resleeving MP reduction

effect.summary: The GM may reduce the morph-point budget for successive resleeves during a mission.

eclipse-phase.rule.repeat-resleeving-mp-.cost_or_limit: Recommended reduction is one MP per subsequent resleeve, before boosts.
eclipse-phase.rule.repeat-resleeving-mp-.who_may: Characters resleeving more than once during a mission.
eclipse-phase.rule.repeat-resleeving-mp-.combines: Resources, rep favors, and negative traits can boost available MP.

eclipse-phase.rule.forking.name: Forking

effect.summary: Copies a transhuman ego and re-instances the copy.

eclipse-phase.rule.forking.cost_or_limit: Forks diverge as time apart increases, making later merging more difficult.
eclipse-phase.rule.forking.go_wrong: Forks may become independent and reject merging or obedience.
eclipse-phase.rule.forking.mind: The copy begins with the source ego’s mental state but can diverge into a separate person.
eclipse-phase.rule.forking.combines: Forks may later be merged with their originating ego.
eclipse-phase.rule.forking.blocked_reason: It creates a distinct continuing person from a copied ego.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-legal-divergence.name: Fork legal divergence

effect.summary: Fork rights and permitted existence vary by polity, with some requiring automatic deletion after a legal divergence period.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-legal-divergence.cost_or_limit: Specific limits differ by jurisdiction; some impose a 48-hour limit or require an erase application.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-legal-divergence.go_wrong: Illegal forks may face deletion or property status.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-legal-divergence.who_may: Forks and their originating egos, as regulated by local polities.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-legal-divergence.combines: Some jurisdictions require an auto-erase app.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-legal-divergence.blocked_reason: It governs a fork’s continued existence and legal identity.

eclipse-phase.rule.neural-pruning-memory.name: Neural pruning memory granularity

effect.summary: Specific memories cannot be selected for excision; edits operate on broad groups, commonly periods of six months or more.

eclipse-phase.rule.neural-pruning-memory.cost_or_limit: Most beta forks lose memories older than one year.
eclipse-phase.rule.neural-pruning-memory.go_wrong: Unintended associated memories may be affected.
eclipse-phase.rule.neural-pruning-memory.mind: Memory content is altered or removed in broad clumps.
eclipse-phase.rule.neural-pruning-memory.blocked_reason: It constrains targeted alterations to stored memories.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-divergence-and-m.name: Fork divergence and merging

effect.summary: Forks become more distinct over time, making reintegration harder and potentially causing stress or lost fork memories.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-divergence-and-m.cost_or_limit: Longer separation increases the difficulty and consequences of merging.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-divergence-and-m.go_wrong: Merge may lose memories and cause mental stress; psychosurgery may address problems later.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-divergence-and-m.mind: Forks develop as separate people as their experiences diverge.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-divergence-and-m.blocked_reason: It governs the continuity and recombination of separate ego instances.

eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery.name: Psychosurgery

effect.summary: Psychosurgery selectively alters a digitized mind in a simulspace.

eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery.cost_or_limit: Requires the subject’s digitized ego, a psychosurgery app, and a server; procedures take task-action time.
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery.go_wrong: Failure may do nothing; critical failure can inflict permanent mental damage, and procedures can impose stress.
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery.mind: Can alter, treat, interrogate, or damage the subject’s mental state.
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery.who_may: Psychosurgeons with the required access and equipment; subjects need not consent.
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery.where_from: A real-time emulation, backup, or fork run in simulspace.
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery.combines: May use external modules, patches, stimulation programs, or time-accelerated test forks.
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery.blocked_reason: It directly and persistently alters a mind, including memory and behavior.

eclipse-phase.rule.neural-pruning-failur.name: Neural pruning failure penalties

effect.summary: Failure in neural pruning gives the beta fork a listed penalty, with more for superior failure; penalties may accumulate.

eclipse-phase.rule.neural-pruning-failur.go_wrong: Skill reduction, ego-trait changes, SV, or extra memory loss may result.
eclipse-phase.rule.neural-pruning-failur.mind: Affects the beta fork's skills, memories, or traits.
eclipse-phase.rule.neural-pruning-failur.blocked_reason: The rule concerns creating a separate forked ego with its own state.

eclipse-phase.rule.identity-is-tied-to-e.name: Identity is tied to ego

effect.summary: An ego ID links identity to the ego and is used for legal and administrative verification.

eclipse-phase.rule.identity-is-tied-to-e.cost_or_limit: Records and checks differ among habitats.
eclipse-phase.rule.identity-is-tied-to-e.go_wrong: Records may be incomplete, inconsistent, or absent.
eclipse-phase.rule.identity-is-tied-to-e.who_may: Authorities and services use the ID; the passage does not set eligibility.
eclipse-phase.rule.identity-is-tied-to-e.combines: ID may be encoded in digital mind-states and morphs.
eclipse-phase.rule.identity-is-tied-to-e.mechanism: Identity credential bound to an ego.
eclipse-phase.rule.identity-is-tied-to-e.blocked_reason: The rule binds identity to an ego across backups, uploads, forks, and resleeving, which needs persistent ego-state rules.

eclipse-phase.rule.ego-id-in-backups-and.name: Ego ID in backups and morphs

effect.summary: Services encode an ego ID hash in digital mind-states, and body banks encode it into a morph as a nanotattoo.

eclipse-phase.rule.ego-id-in-backups-and.cost_or_limit: Many jurisdictions require morphs and embodied IDs to be registered locally.
eclipse-phase.rule.ego-id-in-backups-and.mind: The digital mind-state carries a readable cryptographic identifier.
eclipse-phase.rule.ego-id-in-backups-and.who_may: Backup, upload, egocast, and resleeving services are required to do this in the described system.
eclipse-phase.rule.ego-id-in-backups-and.combines: Links digital identity and physical nanotattoo records.
eclipse-phase.rule.ego-id-in-backups-and.mechanism: Persistent identity metadata in mind-states and morphs.
eclipse-phase.rule.ego-id-in-backups-and.blocked_reason: The rule requires identity to persist as a mind moves between backups, uploads, and bodies.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-identity-designa.name: Fork identity designation

effect.summary: In some polities, a fork's ID must identify its originating ego, fork status, and inception date.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-identity-designa.cost_or_limit: Forks may be barred from travel, transactions, voting, or sleeving without authorization or by law.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-identity-designa.go_wrong: Restrictions aim to deter fraud and unauthorized independence.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-identity-designa.who_may: Applies to forks in polities with legal limits on forks.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-identity-designa.combines: Fork IDs can be linked to an originator's authorization.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-identity-designa.mechanism: Fork status and permissions encoded in identity credentials.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-identity-designa.blocked_reason: This rule depends on distinct fork identities and their relationship to an originating ego.

eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-tied-to-id.name: Reputation tied to ID

effect.summary: Identity and reputation scores are irrevocably linked.

eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-tied-to-id.combines: ID systems may include reputation-system identifiers.
eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-tied-to-id.mechanism: Credential linkage between identity and reputation.
eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-tied-to-id.blocked_reason: This can be represented as a persistent relation between an identity and a reputation record.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanotat-encryption-an.name: Nanotat encryption and signing

effect.summary: Nanotat data may be passcode-protected and is cryptographically signed by the resleeving company's public key.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanotat-encryption-an.cost_or_limit: Authorities may require data to be decoded at security checkpoints.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanotat-encryption-an.go_wrong: Theft devices may crack codes or attackers may take the finger itself.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanotat-encryption-an.who_may: The resleeving company signs the data; authorities may demand access.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanotat-encryption-an.combines: Online records and signature checks can reveal alteration.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanotat-encryption-an.blocked_reason: This is an information access and verification rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.brainprint-similarity.name: Brainprint similarity across morphs

effect.summary: Brain scans can identify an ego across morphs through neural activity and responses to sensory stimuli.

eclipse-phase.rule.brainprint-similarity.cost_or_limit: A full physical scan takes about an hour; virtual-state scans take about five minutes.
eclipse-phase.rule.brainprint-similarity.go_wrong: Hacking the scanner can defeat the otherwise reliable check.
eclipse-phase.rule.brainprint-similarity.mind: Scans measure neural activity and sensory responses.
eclipse-phase.rule.brainprint-similarity.who_may: Security personnel or facilities conducting identity checks.
eclipse-phase.rule.brainprint-similarity.combines: Virtual mind-states use diagnostic inputs instead of the same physical process.
eclipse-phase.rule.brainprint-similarity.blocked_reason: It detects and compares hidden identity information through a specialized scan.

eclipse-phase.rule.brainprint-drift.name: Brainprint drift

effect.summary: Brainprints change gradually with memories, trauma, and adaptation, so they need periodic updating.

eclipse-phase.rule.brainprint-drift.cost_or_limit: Usually requires updating about yearly, sometimes more often.
eclipse-phase.rule.brainprint-drift.go_wrong: Psychological trauma, psychosurgery, infection, or other changes can make a check fail.
eclipse-phase.rule.brainprint-drift.mind: Changes to brain structure and activity alter the print.
eclipse-phase.rule.brainprint-drift.combines: May interact with psychosurgery and exsurgent-virus infection.
eclipse-phase.rule.brainprint-drift.blocked_reason: This is a changing identity measurement that can be recorded and checked.

eclipse-phase.rule.digital-id-code.name: Digital ID code

effect.summary: Backups and infomorphs carry a cryptographically hashed identity code for ownership and resleeving verification.

eclipse-phase.rule.digital-id-code.go_wrong: Forging is difficult but tampering can fail online verification unless encryption is defeated.
eclipse-phase.rule.digital-id-code.mind: The code is stored with the digital mind-state.
eclipse-phase.rule.digital-id-code.combines: Contains information comparable to a nanotat ID.
eclipse-phase.rule.digital-id-code.blocked_reason: The rule makes an identity credential persist with backups and infomorphs.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanotat-alteration-an.name: Nanotat alteration and replacement

effect.summary: Nanobot treatments can erase, rewrite, or replace nanotat identity data.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanotat-alteration-an.cost_or_limit: Erasing is easy but may itself be suspicious or illegal; rewriting fails online checks unless encryption is cracked.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanotat-alteration-an.go_wrong: Altered data may fail authorization checks.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanotat-alteration-an.combines: Fake IDs may be installed as replacements.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanotat-alteration-an.blocked_reason: It changes information stored in an identity mark.

eclipse-phase.rule.digital-id-tampering.name: Digital ID tampering

effect.summary: Digital identity codes can be modified, but altered codes fail online checks unless encryption is also defeated.

eclipse-phase.rule.digital-id-tampering.cost_or_limit: Requires defeating encryption to preserve verification.
eclipse-phase.rule.digital-id-tampering.go_wrong: The ID may fail online verification.

eclipse-phase.rule.egocasting-range-and-.name: Egocasting range and transit

effect.summary: Quantum farcasting transfers an ego over interplanetary distances at light speed, with travel time set by distance.

eclipse-phase.rule.egocasting-range-and-.cost_or_limit: Most people egocast for trips longer than 1.5 million kilometers; times range from minutes locally to many hours or longer across the Solar System.
eclipse-phase.rule.egocasting-range-and-.mind: The ego is transferred, not the physical body.
eclipse-phase.rule.egocasting-range-and-.where_from: Egocasting combines uploading and quantum farcasting.
eclipse-phase.rule.egocasting-range-and-.combines: The arriving ego may be active, a backup, or an upload from a conscious mind.
eclipse-phase.rule.egocasting-range-and-.blocked_reason: The passage describes transfer of an ego between physical locations and mind-state forms.

eclipse-phase.rule.egocaster-security-ri.name: Egocaster security risk

effect.summary: A compromised or untrusted farcaster service can meddle with the ego it handles.

eclipse-phase.rule.egocaster-security-ri.cost_or_limit: Breaches are uncommon under ordinary strict security practices.
eclipse-phase.rule.egocaster-security-ri.go_wrong: Political extremists or criminal operators may abuse access to the transmitted ego.
eclipse-phase.rule.egocaster-security-ri.mind: The transmitted ego may be altered or otherwise meddled with.
eclipse-phase.rule.egocaster-security-ri.combines: Risk exists at either end of the transfer.
eclipse-phase.rule.egocaster-security-ri.blocked_reason: This rule concerns custody and alteration of a mind during transfer.

eclipse-phase.rule.cold-storage-of-egos.name: Cold storage of egos

effect.summary: Station authorities may archive an arriving ego or keep it in cold storage instead of allowing it to resleeve.

eclipse-phase.rule.cold-storage-of-egos.cost_or_limit: Authorities control the destination receiver and may impose screening.
eclipse-phase.rule.cold-storage-of-egos.go_wrong: An ego may have little recourse against detention.
eclipse-phase.rule.cold-storage-of-egos.mind: The ego may be prevented from acting or resleeving.
eclipse-phase.rule.cold-storage-of-egos.combines: May follow interviews or psychosurgery interrogation.
eclipse-phase.rule.cold-storage-of-egos.blocked_reason: The rule requires a stored ego to remain a distinct, controllable mind-state.

eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery-interro.name: Psychosurgery interrogation of arrivals

effect.summary: Some habitats may use harsh psychosurgery interrogation on suspect arriving infomorphs.

eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery-interro.go_wrong: The treatment may be invasive and the ego may be unable to refuse effectively.
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery-interro.mind: May subject an arriving mind to psychosurgery.
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery-interro.combines: Can follow a simulspace interview and identity check.
eclipse-phase.rule.psychosurgery-interro.blocked_reason: The procedure can invasively alter or interrogate a mind under authority control.

eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-interlock.name: Airlock interlock

effect.summary: Airlock controls prevent opening both doors at once to avoid accidental depressurization.

eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-interlock.cost_or_limit: A door takes one action turn to open or close; cycling air takes at least three action turns.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-interlock.go_wrong: Overriding or malfunctioning safety sensors can allow injury or death.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-interlock.combines: Pressurized-area doors work as ordinary doors until a module is depressurized.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-interlock.blocked_reason: The rule depends on pressure containment and linked door states.

eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-obstruction-a.name: Airlock obstruction and injury

effect.summary: A person caught in a closing airlock can be severely injured or killed, especially if the head, neck, or vitals are trapped.

eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-obstruction-a.cost_or_limit: A safety override or malfunction is needed for the lock to close on someone.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-obstruction-a.go_wrong: The described injury is DV 3d10 + 10 and usually dismembers; vital areas being caught means certain death.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-obstruction-a.who_may: Applies to people caught in an airlock.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-obstruction-a.combines: Hardwired sensors are intended to prevent closure on people or objects.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-obstruction-a.mechanism: Crushing hazard from a closing pressure door.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-obstruction-a.blocked_reason: The outcome can be represented as an immediate harmful effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-fire-response.name: Airlock fire response

effect.summary: Linked heat and carbon monoxide sensors close an air gap and can let operations remotely blow the lock to suppress a fire.

eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-fire-response.cost_or_limit: Requires linked sensors and remote operations access.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-fire-response.combines: Uses heat and carbon monoxide sensors.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-fire-response.blocked_reason: It depends on environmental sensors and compartment-wide fire isolation.

eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-blowout.name: Airlock blowout

effect.summary: Opening an outer airlock without cycling vents its atmosphere rapidly and can blow nearby people or loose objects outward.

eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-blowout.cost_or_limit: The venting takes half the normal cycling time; danger extends 25 meters, or 50 for large locks.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-blowout.go_wrong: People may be pulled out at 20 meters per turn, or 40 for large locks; flying debris can injure them.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-blowout.who_may: Applies when an airlock is blown outward.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-blowout.combines: Checks to hold on are modified by liquid environments or advance warning; open doors can keep venting until pressure is minimal.
eclipse-phase.rule.airlock-blowout.blocked_reason: The outcome depends on a changing pressure field affecting people and objects throughout an area.

eclipse-phase.rule.high-pressure-decompr.name: High-pressure decompression

effect.summary: An abrupt pressure change in a high-pressure environment can crush or kill occupants and catastrophically damage the surrounding structure.

eclipse-phase.rule.high-pressure-decompr.cost_or_limit: Applies in environments such as Venus's surface or Europa's subsurface ocean.
eclipse-phase.rule.high-pressure-decompr.go_wrong: Occupants and the structure can be destroyed by the pressure change.
eclipse-phase.rule.high-pressure-decompr.who_may: Applies to anything inside an affected airlock.
eclipse-phase.rule.high-pressure-decompr.combines: Survival gear and morphs are engineered for the environment but not abrupt pressure changes.
eclipse-phase.rule.high-pressure-decompr.blocked_reason: The rule applies environmental pressure damage to people and structures across an affected area.

eclipse-phase.rule.bulkhead-isolation.name: Bulkhead isolation

effect.summary: Bulkheads isolate sections of a habitat or ship during depressurization, outbreaks, invasions, or emergencies.

eclipse-phase.rule.bulkhead-isolation.cost_or_limit: Bulkheads follow airlock rules except they do not need time to cycle air.
eclipse-phase.rule.bulkhead-isolation.combines: Installed at strategic locations to divide a structure into sections.
eclipse-phase.rule.bulkhead-isolation.blocked_reason: The rule requires sealed sections and environmental containment.

eclipse-phase.rule.life-support-maintena.name: Life-support maintenance

effect.summary: Modern life support can run indefinitely if maintained and not disrupted.

eclipse-phase.rule.life-support-maintena.cost_or_limit: Requires regular maintenance and uninterrupted operation.
eclipse-phase.rule.life-support-maintena.go_wrong: Interference can compromise atmosphere and other life-support functions.
eclipse-phase.rule.life-support-maintena.where_from: Modern ship and habitat life support
eclipse-phase.rule.life-support-maintena.blocked_reason: A maintenance condition is directly usable as a game constraint.

eclipse-phase.rule.algae-breach-atmosphe.name: Algae breach atmosphere loss

effect.summary: After a breach, air typically becomes unbreathable within 48–72 hours at full capacity, more slowly with fewer breathers.

eclipse-phase.rule.algae-breach-atmosphe.cost_or_limit: Timing depends on system volume and the number of biomorphs aboard.
eclipse-phase.rule.algae-breach-atmosphe.go_wrong: Atmosphere loss may lead to asphyxiation.
eclipse-phase.rule.algae-breach-atmosphe.blocked_reason: The changing atmosphere and time window can be represented with basic effects and a countdown.

eclipse-phase.rule.reactor-emergency-shu.name: Reactor emergency shutdown

effect.summary: An emergency safe shutdown requires an Interface test and a complex action, then takes two action turns.

eclipse-phase.rule.reactor-emergency-shu.cost_or_limit: A gradual safe shutdown takes 6–12 hours.
eclipse-phase.rule.reactor-emergency-shu.go_wrong: Disabling safety protocols to trigger a meltdown is difficult and dangerous.
eclipse-phase.rule.reactor-emergency-shu.who_may: A character able to access reactor controls
eclipse-phase.rule.reactor-emergency-shu.combines: Controls are air-gapped, hardwired, and well defended.
eclipse-phase.rule.reactor-emergency-shu.blocked_reason: The procedure is represented by ordinary tests and elapsed time.

eclipse-phase.rule.reactor-containment-b.name: Reactor containment breach

effect.summary: A breach releases superheated plasma that can burn people nearby and floods the area with heavy radiation.

eclipse-phase.rule.reactor-containment-b.cost_or_limit: The plasma burn affects those within 10 meters who fail a Fray test.
eclipse-phase.rule.reactor-containment-b.go_wrong: Radiation is usually lethal to biomorphs; damaged pressurized steam systems may explode.
eclipse-phase.rule.reactor-containment-b.combines: Plasma breaches can damage nearby steam systems and turbines.
eclipse-phase.rule.reactor-containment-b.blocked_reason: The simultaneous area-wide radiation and proximity-based plasma hazard needs area-field handling.

eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-score-tran.name: Reputation score transactions

effect.summary: Positive interactions increase reputation and negative interactions reduce it, with transactions weighted by context.

eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-score-tran.cost_or_limit: Networks differ in weighting and monitor attempts to manipulate scores.
eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-score-tran.go_wrong: Reputation can reinforce informal hierarchies, prejudice, or cliques.
eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-score-tran.combines: Muse automation may process transactions based on habits and reactions.
eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-score-tran.blocked_reason: Persistent changes to a social standing measure fit the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-is-not-spe.name: Reputation is not spent

effect.summary: In the inner system, reputation measures social capital rather than functioning as currency.

eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-is-not-spe.cost_or_limit: Reputation can open doors and provide privileges but is not ordinarily spent.
eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-is-not-spe.combines: Outer-system reputation emphasizes trust and solidarity.
eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-is-not-spe.blocked_reason: This is a constraint on how reputation may be used.

eclipse-phase.rule.rep-favor-limits.name: Rep favor limits

effect.summary: The number of favors safely requested is limited by favor level and refresh period.

eclipse-phase.rule.rep-favor-limits.cost_or_limit: A higher-level favor can substitute, or reputation can be burned; failed tests usually do not consume a favor except on critical failure.
eclipse-phase.rule.rep-favor-limits.go_wrong: Burning reputation reduces the character’s score.
eclipse-phase.rule.rep-favor-limits.combines: Favor availability refreshes on level-specific timeframes.
eclipse-phase.rule.rep-favor-limits.blocked_reason: The rule is a straightforward per-period resource limit.

eclipse-phase.rule.burning-reputation.name: Burning reputation

effect.summary: A character can lose reputation to gain an extra favor or a bonus on a Rep test.

eclipse-phase.rule.burning-reputation.cost_or_limit: The bonus is twice the burned points, capped at +30.
eclipse-phase.rule.burning-reputation.go_wrong: People may regard the character as demanding, lowering reputation.
eclipse-phase.rule.burning-reputation.combines: May be used for an additional favor or a test modifier.
eclipse-phase.rule.burning-reputation.blocked_reason: The tradeoff is a direct numerical change and test bonus.

eclipse-phase.rule.keeping-quiet-about-f.name: Keeping quiet about favors

effect.summary: Negative modifiers used to keep a request discreet also hinder tests to learn about it.

eclipse-phase.rule.keeping-quiet-about-f.cost_or_limit: A smaller pool of trusted people makes the favor harder to obtain.
eclipse-phase.rule.keeping-quiet-about-f.go_wrong: Mesh monitoring can reveal a user’s normal reputation identity.
eclipse-phase.rule.keeping-quiet-about-f.combines: Applies the same negative modifier to attempts to investigate the activity.
eclipse-phase.rule.keeping-quiet-about-f.blocked_reason: Concealment and its mirrored penalty can be represented with ordinary modifiers.

eclipse-phase.rule.false-identity-reputa.name: False identity reputation

effect.summary: A false identity has its own separately tracked, usually low reputation score that can be built up.

eclipse-phase.rule.false-identity-reputa.cost_or_limit: The usual starting score is about 10; using a normal score while undercover can expose the user.
eclipse-phase.rule.false-identity-reputa.go_wrong: Mesh monitoring may reveal the character’s activity.
eclipse-phase.rule.false-identity-reputa.combines: Optional rules allow character-generation points to improve a new false identity’s score.
eclipse-phase.rule.false-identity-reputa.blocked_reason: Separate scores can be tracked as distinct character values.

eclipse-phase.rule.gear-quality-and-comp.name: Gear quality and complexity

effect.summary: Gear quality modifies task outcomes, and each +10 quality bonus raises complexity by one step.

eclipse-phase.rule.gear-quality-and-comp.cost_or_limit: Poor quality imposes penalties; ordinary gear is assumed average quality.
eclipse-phase.rule.gear-quality-and-comp.go_wrong: Quality can decline through use and circumstances.
eclipse-phase.rule.gear-quality-and-comp.combines: Gear modifiers are usually cumulative unless effects duplicate.
eclipse-phase.rule.gear-quality-and-comp.blocked_reason: The rule uses ordinary modifiers and item classifications.

eclipse-phase.rule.gear-compatibility-wi.name: Gear compatibility with morphology

effect.summary: Gear made for a different morphology can impose penalties or be unusable.

eclipse-phase.rule.gear-compatibility-wi.cost_or_limit: The impairment is usually −10 to −30, at the GM’s discretion.
eclipse-phase.rule.gear-compatibility-wi.go_wrong: The character may be unable to use the equipment.
eclipse-phase.rule.gear-compatibility-wi.who_may: Users whose morphology differs from the gear design
eclipse-phase.rule.gear-compatibility-wi.combines: Gear designs can be made for uplifts, nonhumanoids, and unusual limbs.
eclipse-phase.rule.gear-compatibility-wi.blocked_reason: The passage specifies direct usability limits and task penalties.

eclipse-phase.rule.meshed-gear-vulnerabi.name: Meshed gear vulnerability

effect.summary: Meshed devices can be tracked over the mesh and are vulnerable to hacking, subject to their protections.

eclipse-phase.rule.meshed-gear-vulnerabi.cost_or_limit: Firewalls and device ALIs provide protection.
eclipse-phase.rule.meshed-gear-vulnerabi.combines: Devices may be puppeted through mesh inserts or ectos.
eclipse-phase.rule.meshed-gear-vulnerabi.blocked_reason: Tracking and intrusion are representable as information and working effects.

eclipse-phase.rule.device-power-enduranc.name: Device power endurance

effect.summary: Standard batteries last 100–500 hours, while shielded nuclear batteries last three years or more.

eclipse-phase.rule.device-power-enduranc.cost_or_limit: Power is usually not an issue unless the plot or a critical failure makes it relevant.
eclipse-phase.rule.device-power-enduranc.go_wrong: Devices may fail when power is exhausted or disrupted.
eclipse-phase.rule.device-power-enduranc.combines: Nuclear batteries may recharge standard batteries; transmitters can charge devices wirelessly.
eclipse-phase.rule.device-power-enduranc.blocked_reason: Battery duration is a straightforward resource limit.

eclipse-phase.rule.ware-availability-by-.name: Ware availability by morph

effect.summary: Different ware categories are restricted to particular morph types, and each item normally installs only once per morph.

eclipse-phase.rule.ware-availability-by-.cost_or_limit: Bioware and cyberware require biomorphs; hardware requires synthetic shells, bots, or vehicles; meshware targets infomorphs; nanoware is broadly available.
eclipse-phase.rule.ware-availability-by-.who_may: Users meeting the category’s morph requirement
eclipse-phase.rule.ware-availability-by-.combines: Nanoware can be used by morphs of all types.
eclipse-phase.rule.ware-availability-by-.blocked_reason: The rule requires tracking installation state and enforcing a per-morph carry limit.

eclipse-phase.rule.mission-gear-points.name: Mission Gear Points

effect.summary: Characters receive a mission allocation of Gear Points to acquire equipment, and unused points expire after preparation.

eclipse-phase.rule.mission-gear-points.cost_or_limit: The suggested allocation is 20 points; gear costs depend on complexity, and the GM may restrict eligible gear.
eclipse-phase.rule.mission-gear-points.go_wrong: Availability may be limited by location, resources, restrictions, or urgency.
eclipse-phase.rule.mission-gear-points.combines: Resources and rep favors can increase the allocation.
eclipse-phase.rule.mission-gear-points.blocked_reason: A limited acquisition budget is directly usable as a game resource.

eclipse-phase.rule.rep-favors-for-gear.name: Rep favors for gear

effect.summary: A minor, moderate, or major favor grants 1, 2, or 3 Gear Points respectively.

eclipse-phase.rule.rep-favors-for-gear.cost_or_limit: Requires at least 40 reputation in a network relevant to the situation; use counts against mission favors.
eclipse-phase.rule.rep-favors-for-gear.go_wrong: An unsuitable network may not help acquire the item.
eclipse-phase.rule.rep-favors-for-gear.who_may: Characters with an applicable reputation score
eclipse-phase.rule.rep-favors-for-gear.combines: May be used with other Gear Point sources.
eclipse-phase.rule.rep-favors-for-gear.blocked_reason: The rule is a direct conversion into a limited resource.

eclipse-phase.rule.gear-acquisition-time.name: Gear acquisition timeframes

effect.summary: Acquired gear takes time according to complexity, with digital-only goods usually taking one minute.

eclipse-phase.rule.gear-acquisition-time.cost_or_limit: Physical items generally take two hours for Minor, eight for Moderate, and 24 for Major; Rare or Restricted timing is up to the GM.
eclipse-phase.rule.gear-acquisition-time.go_wrong: Local availability, shipping, lag, disruption, or censorship can delay acquisition.
eclipse-phase.rule.gear-acquisition-time.combines: Multiple items add their timeframes together.
eclipse-phase.rule.gear-acquisition-time.blocked_reason: The rule specifies elapsed time rather than an unsupported effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.single-use-blueprints.name: Single-use blueprints

effect.summary: A single-use blueprint allows one print and prevents copying or further use.

eclipse-phase.rule.single-use-blueprints.cost_or_limit: Obtained through Gear Points, reputation, or Resources using the item’s complexity.
eclipse-phase.rule.single-use-blueprints.go_wrong: Some files erase themselves after use.
eclipse-phase.rule.single-use-blueprints.who_may: Licensed users or holders of the file
eclipse-phase.rule.single-use-blueprints.combines: Digital rights management enforces use limits.
eclipse-phase.rule.single-use-blueprints.blocked_reason: A blueprint use count can be tracked as a simple resource.

eclipse-phase.rule.limited-use-blueprint.name: Limited-use blueprints

effect.summary: Recycling a printed item in a licensed fabber grants a credit for another print.

eclipse-phase.rule.limited-use-blueprint.cost_or_limit: Requires the relevant licensed recycler and a credit from disassembly.
eclipse-phase.rule.limited-use-blueprint.combines: The credit permits another print of the same item.
eclipse-phase.rule.limited-use-blueprint.blocked_reason: The recycle-and-credit loop can be tracked with a simple resource.

eclipse-phase.rule.multi-use-blueprints.name: Multi-use blueprints

effect.summary: A multi-use blueprint permits repeated printing and copying but is keyed to its owner’s identity.

eclipse-phase.rule.multi-use-blueprints.cost_or_limit: Normally costs one complexity step more; Major versions are rare and largely unavailable.
eclipse-phase.rule.multi-use-blueprints.combines: An owner may print the item repeatedly.
eclipse-phase.rule.multi-use-blueprints.blocked_reason: Identity-locked reuse is not represented by the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.open-source-blueprint.name: Open-source blueprints

effect.summary: Open-source designs can be reused and copied without identity authentication.

eclipse-phase.rule.open-source-blueprint.cost_or_limit: May require research or a favor; some designs are illegal or incompatible with local fabbers.
eclipse-phase.rule.open-source-blueprint.go_wrong: Research-acquired designs have a 20% chance of being unreliable, buggy, or malicious.
eclipse-phase.rule.open-source-blueprint.who_may: Users who can obtain the design
eclipse-phase.rule.open-source-blueprint.where_from: Autonomist regions and other open libraries
eclipse-phase.rule.open-source-blueprint.combines: Some prints may carry malware or work poorly on inner-system fabricators.
eclipse-phase.rule.open-source-blueprint.blocked_reason: Copying and using a design fits the basic information effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.restricted-item-fabri.name: Restricted-item fabrication

effect.summary: Restricted-item designs generally cannot be legally bought with Resources or printed by inner-system fabbers without proper licensing.

eclipse-phase.rule.restricted-item-fabri.cost_or_limit: Illegal purchases or hacking may bypass the restrictions.
eclipse-phase.rule.restricted-item-fabri.go_wrong: Unauthorized attempts may be detected or prevented.
eclipse-phase.rule.restricted-item-fabri.who_may: Licensed users or those who bypass controls
eclipse-phase.rule.restricted-item-fabri.combines: Fabber security checks licensing and restriction status.
eclipse-phase.rule.restricted-item-fabri.blocked_reason: The restriction is a direct availability and access-control rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.blueprint-writing-and.name: Blueprint writing and cracking

effect.summary: Creating a design requires an appropriate skill test and Program test; breaking copy restrictions requires a prolonged Program test.

eclipse-phase.rule.blueprint-writing-and.cost_or_limit: Writing generally takes months by item complexity; cracking takes six months or three days in accelerated VR.
eclipse-phase.rule.blueprint-writing-and.go_wrong: Failure may leave the user without a usable design or cracked file.
eclipse-phase.rule.blueprint-writing-and.who_may: Characters with relevant design and programming capability
eclipse-phase.rule.blueprint-writing-and.combines: Forks and accelerated simulspaces can reduce subjective programming time.
eclipse-phase.rule.blueprint-writing-and.blocked_reason: These tasks resolve through tests and elapsed time.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanofabrication-feeds.name: Nanofabrication feedstock

effect.summary: Disassemblers can turn available objects into raw molecular feedstock for printing.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanofabrication-feeds.cost_or_limit: Rare materials or large amounts of a material may be difficult to obtain.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanofabrication-feeds.go_wrong: A print can be delayed or prevented by missing feedstock.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanofabrication-feeds.who_may: Users with access to a capable nanofabricator
eclipse-phase.rule.nanofabrication-feeds.where_from: Habitat recycling, feedlines, and raw-material supplies
eclipse-phase.rule.nanofabrication-feeds.blocked_reason: The conversion depends on tracking and supplying specific materials beyond the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.sensory-databases.name: Sensory databases

effect.summary: Recognition databases can improve identification of sensed objects or creatures.

eclipse-phase.rule.sensory-databases.cost_or_limit: Grants +10 to relevant Perceive and Know tests.
eclipse-phase.rule.sensory-databases.who_may: Users of technological sensors or enhanced biological senses.
eclipse-phase.rule.sensory-databases.where_from: Sensor databases may be implant-based, online, or mesh-stored.
eclipse-phase.rule.sensory-databases.combines: Pairs sensory input with signature matching.
eclipse-phase.rule.sensory-databases.blocked_reason: The rule is a straightforward information bonus.

eclipse-phase.rule.active-vs-passive.name: Active vs. Passive

effect.summary: Active sensors emit signals that comparable sensors may detect; passive sensors only receive naturally occurring signals.

eclipse-phase.rule.active-vs-passive.cost_or_limit: Active scanning can expose and attract attention to its source.
eclipse-phase.rule.active-vs-passive.combines: Applies to the listed scanning technologies.

eclipse-phase.rule.soundwaves.name: Soundwaves

effect.summary: Sound travels through a medium but does not propagate in vacuum.

eclipse-phase.rule.soundwaves.cost_or_limit: Infrasound travels farther than ordinary sound; ultrasound supports echolocation.
eclipse-phase.rule.soundwaves.who_may: Applies to sound and sound-based sensors.
eclipse-phase.rule.soundwaves.blocked_reason: The rule is a straightforward environmental constraint.

eclipse-phase.rule.living-creatures-cann.name: Living creatures cannot be nanofabricated

effect.summary: Creatures must be acquired through Resources or reputation rather than nanofabrication.

eclipse-phase.rule.living-creatures-cann.blocked_reason: This is a setting restriction on producing living creatures.

eclipse-phase.rule.training-and-commandi.name: Training and commanding creatures

effect.summary: Creature training and control use Exotic Skill: Animal Handling.

eclipse-phase.rule.training-and-commandi.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward skill-based control rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.antidote-creation.name: Antidote creation

effect.summary: A sample, medical shop, and one-hour pharmacology task can produce an antidote for most toxins.

eclipse-phase.rule.antidote-creation.cost_or_limit: Requires a toxin sample and medical shop; takes one hour.
eclipse-phase.rule.antidote-creation.who_may: Characters able to perform the pharmacology task.
eclipse-phase.rule.antidote-creation.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward task-based rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.neutrino-transmission.name: Neutrino transmission

effect.summary: Neutrinos pass through solid matter and cannot be blocked, but broadcasts can be intercepted by a receiver behind the intended destination.

eclipse-phase.rule.neutrino-transmission.cost_or_limit: Generating broadcasts requires a large power plant.
eclipse-phase.rule.neutrino-transmission.combines: Often paired with quantum farcasting for security.
eclipse-phase.rule.neutrino-transmission.mechanism: Unblocked particle communication with interception risk.
eclipse-phase.rule.neutrino-transmission.blocked_reason: This is a world mechanism that can be implemented as transmission and interception rules.

eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-entangled-com.name: Quantum-entangled communication

effect.summary: Paired reservoirs exchange data instantaneously at any distance, consuming one qubit for each bit sent.

eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-entangled-com.cost_or_limit: Communication stops when either side runs out of matching qubits; producing and transporting them is costly.
eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-entangled-com.go_wrong: An empty reservoir prevents further communication until replenished.
eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-entangled-com.who_may: Users with compatible communicators and matching entangled qubits.
eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-entangled-com.combines: QE communicators require reservoirs containing matching entangled qubits.
eclipse-phase.rule.quantum-entangled-com.blocked_reason: A finite per-message resource can be represented as a usage cost and limit.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanobot-operating-env.name: Nanobot operating environments

effect.summary: Most manufacturing and replication nanobots require maintained environments such as fabbers or healing vats.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanobot-operating-env.blocked_reason: The rule restricts where nanobots can operate.

eclipse-phase.rule.blueprint-and-feedsto.name: Blueprint and feedstock requirement

effect.summary: Fabricators require raw materials and electronic plans to make items.

eclipse-phase.rule.blueprint-and-feedsto.cost_or_limit: Blueprint access may be licensed or restricted; common-use plans are typically included.
eclipse-phase.rule.blueprint-and-feedsto.go_wrong: Programmed restrictions may prevent unlicensed or restricted-item manufacture.
eclipse-phase.rule.blueprint-and-feedsto.combines: Disassemblers can convert unwanted nonliving matter into feedstock.
eclipse-phase.rule.blueprint-and-feedsto.blocked_reason: The rule defines requirements for manufacturing.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-unit-size-and-d.name: Swarm unit size and durability

effect.summary: A standard swarm unit has DUR 25 and DR 50 and occupies up to about 250 cubic meters when fully dispersed; a swarmanoid is twice that size and durability.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-unit-size-and-d.cost_or_limit: Dispersing beyond the stated volume impairs initiative and actions.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-unit-size-and-d.go_wrong: Over-dispersion hinders mite communication and coordination.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-unit-size-and-d.blocked_reason: This rule sets swarm statistics and a coordination limit.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-splitting-and-c.name: Swarm splitting and combining

effect.summary: Splitting divides durability, damage, and independent action among units; merging same-type swarms combines them.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-splitting-and-c.cost_or_limit: Split units divide current durability and damage.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-splitting-and-c.combines: Only swarms of the same type merge.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-splitting-and-c.blocked_reason: This rule governs how swarm units divide or aggregate.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-movement-and-co.name: Swarm movement and collection

effect.summary: Swarms move slowly, move at half speed in vacuum, treat liquids as difficult movement, and can be recollected in about a minute.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-movement-and-co.cost_or_limit: High-speed winds or liquids can hinder or carry swarms away.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-movement-and-co.combines: Canisters and hives disperse swarms rapidly.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-movement-and-co.blocked_reason: This rule defines movement and collection limits.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-mass-limit.name: Swarm mass limit

effect.summary: Swarms cannot lift, carry, or move objects heavier than half a kilogram and cannot make strength checks.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-mass-limit.blocked_reason: This rule restricts swarm strength and carrying capacity.

eclipse-phase.rule.biological-penetratio.name: Biological penetration limit

effect.summary: Swarms cannot effectively penetrate biological forms, though they can attack externally.

eclipse-phase.rule.biological-penetratio.cost_or_limit: Internal biological effects are left to nanoware, nanodrugs, and nanotoxins.
eclipse-phase.rule.biological-penetratio.blocked_reason: This rule restricts swarm effects against living forms.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-environmental-v.name: Swarm environmental vulnerability

effect.summary: Winds above 60 kph damage swarms; prolonged heat above 35 C may damage or incapacitate them, while vacuum does not affect them apart from movement.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-environmental-v.cost_or_limit: High winds deal at least 1d10 damage per turn.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-environmental-v.blocked_reason: This rule establishes environmental damage and immunity.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-combat-resistan.name: Swarm combat resistance

effect.summary: Swarms resist wounds, called shots, grappling, knockdown, and shock; area attacks, fire, plasma, and vehicle collisions deal half damage.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-combat-resistan.cost_or_limit: EMP and adhesive attacks deal 3d10 damage and impose cumulative action penalties until repaired; other attacks deal one damage.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-combat-resistan.go_wrong: Damage and action penalties accumulate until repaired.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-combat-resistan.combines: Attack types have different interactions with swarms.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-combat-resistan.blocked_reason: The rule assigns distinct interactions between swarms and multiple attack types.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-attack-exposure.name: Swarm attack exposure

effect.summary: Swarm attacks affect targets throughout the swarm's volume, bypass armor unless it is environmentally sealed, and blind targets; swarms take one damage per target each turn.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-attack-exposure.cost_or_limit: Nanoswarms generally do not attack conventionally; some have automatic attack effects.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-attack-exposure.go_wrong: Combat damages the swarm for each target engaged.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-attack-exposure.blocked_reason: The rule applies attacks to all targets within a swarm's volume.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-attrition.name: Swarm attrition

effect.summary: A deployed swarm loses five damage daily, or 10–20 in adverse environments; a hive replenishes mites, and a swarm is ineffective at its durability.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-attrition.cost_or_limit: Without a hive, a unit lasts about five days.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-attrition.go_wrong: Accumulated damage disables the swarm at its durability.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-attrition.blocked_reason: Swarm operation depletes over time and hive equipment replenishes it.

eclipse-phase.rule.vehicle-operation.name: Vehicle operation

effect.summary: Most vehicles are piloted by ALI, can be remotely operated, and need a cyberbrain system to sleeve into.

eclipse-phase.rule.vehicle-operation.cost_or_limit: Manual piloting is possible, but is treated as an emergency or personal preference.
eclipse-phase.rule.vehicle-operation.who_may: ALI operators, remote operators, and pilots; sleeving requires added hardware.
eclipse-phase.rule.vehicle-operation.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward restriction on control and inhabitation.

eclipse-phase.rule.common-vehicle-equipm.name: Common vehicle equipment

effect.summary: Vehicles generally include access jacks, mesh inserts, puppet socks, radar, and environmental provisions for closed compartments.

eclipse-phase.rule.common-vehicle-equipm.cost_or_limit: Closed compartments use a breather or 48-hour life support; planetary protection varies by intended environment.
eclipse-phase.rule.common-vehicle-equipm.combines: Mercury, Venus, and Titan designs receive different protective systems.
eclipse-phase.rule.common-vehicle-equipm.mechanism: Default vehicle equipment and environmental protection.
eclipse-phase.rule.common-vehicle-equipm.blocked_reason: The equipment and environmental limits can be tracked as ordinary item properties.

eclipse-phase.rule.hardsuit-protection.name: Hardsuit protection

effect.summary: Hardsuits protect against vacuum, radiation, and extreme temperatures and seal small punctures.

eclipse-phase.rule.hardsuit-protection.cost_or_limit: Punctures below 30 damage self-seal; occupants can wear only armor with AV 4 or less inside.
eclipse-phase.rule.hardsuit-protection.go_wrong: Larger punctures do not receive the stated automatic sealing.
eclipse-phase.rule.hardsuit-protection.combines: Environmental protection and worn armor restrictions.
eclipse-phase.rule.hardsuit-protection.blocked_reason: The description requires a containment capability that protects an occupant from environmental hazards.

eclipse-phase.rule.spacecraft-combat.name: Spacecraft combat

effect.summary: Spacecraft combat is recommended as a plot device because of its extreme lethality; spacecraft weapon damage uses size-based multipliers if needed.

eclipse-phase.rule.spacecraft-combat.cost_or_limit: Weapon DV multiplier is x3 for small craft, x5 for medium craft, and x10 for larger craft.
eclipse-phase.rule.spacecraft-combat.mechanism: Space combat lethality and damage scaling.
eclipse-phase.rule.spacecraft-combat.blocked_reason: The rule can be applied as a damage multiplier and encounter constraint.

eclipse-phase.rule.crime-evidence-and-tr.name: Crime evidence and tracking

effect.summary: A poorly concealed crime can be identified and its perpetrator located quickly using setting technology.

eclipse-phase.rule.crime-evidence-and-tr.combines: Mesh and surveillance technology support identification.
eclipse-phase.rule.crime-evidence-and-tr.blocked_reason: This is an information and tracking mechanism.

eclipse-phase.rule.older-backup-restorat.name: Older backup restoration

effect.summary: Restoration from an older backup reverts a character to that recorded state, potentially losing memories and Rez points.

eclipse-phase.rule.older-backup-restorat.cost_or_limit: The character returns only to the backup’s recorded state.
eclipse-phase.rule.older-backup-restorat.go_wrong: Later memories and advancement may be absent.
eclipse-phase.rule.older-backup-restorat.mind: The restored ego may lack subsequent memories.
eclipse-phase.rule.older-backup-restorat.combines: Cortical stacks and backup agreements determine restoration.
eclipse-phase.rule.older-backup-restorat.blocked_reason: A basic effect grammar does not represent ego-state rollback and the resulting memory loss.

eclipse-phase.rule.forking-as-reproducti.name: Forking as reproduction

effect.summary: Forking is treated as reproduction, and excessive self-replication is widely restricted by law and custom.

eclipse-phase.rule.forking-as-reproducti.cost_or_limit: Large fork populations can draw penalties or lack legal status.
eclipse-phase.rule.forking-as-reproducti.go_wrong: Fork hordes can provoke complaints, lawsuits, or mercenary action.
eclipse-phase.rule.forking-as-reproducti.combines: Resource and territory use affects social response.
eclipse-phase.rule.forking-as-reproducti.blocked_reason: The passage states a social and legal restriction rather than an unmodeled supernatural effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-self-preservatio.name: Fork self-preservation

effect.summary: Forks separated for long periods may develop a drive to preserve themselves.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-self-preservatio.cost_or_limit: The tendency can emerge over time apart.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-self-preservatio.go_wrong: Forks may become troublesome or rebel.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-self-preservatio.mind: Separation can produce self-preservation and independent interests.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-self-preservatio.blocked_reason: Modeling a fork’s independent self-preservation and possible rebellion exceeds basic effects.

eclipse-phase.rule.time-accelerated-simu.name: Time-accelerated simulspace

effect.summary: A simulspace can greatly accelerate subjective time for its occupants.

eclipse-phase.rule.time-accelerated-simu.cost_or_limit: Requires access to substantial computing resources; it cannot replace precise simulation or real skill development.
eclipse-phase.rule.time-accelerated-simu.go_wrong: Fork labor may create resentment or rebellion.
eclipse-phase.rule.time-accelerated-simu.mind: Forks may resent extended virtual labor.
eclipse-phase.rule.time-accelerated-simu.combines: Can be used by forks, but does not make inaccurate simulations reliable.
eclipse-phase.rule.time-accelerated-simu.blocked_reason: Accelerated subjective time requires a time-rate change beyond the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanofabrication-feeds.name: Nanofabrication feedstock limits

effect.summary: Personal-scale fabrication is ordinary, but industrial quantities are costly, complicated, and may exceed local supplies.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanofabrication-feeds.cost_or_limit: Rare elements and surplus feedstock are limited.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanofabrication-feeds.go_wrong: Large requests may be rejected, inspected, or draw attention.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanofabrication-feeds.blocked_reason: This is a resource and access constraint.

eclipse-phase.rule.weapons-of-mass-destr.name: Weapons of mass destruction detection

effect.summary: Most weapons of mass destruction are reliably detectable by transhuman sensors.

eclipse-phase.rule.weapons-of-mass-destr.cost_or_limit: Moving them into or out of habitats can be difficult.
eclipse-phase.rule.weapons-of-mass-destr.go_wrong: Frequent use can lead to being hunted as a suspected terrorist.
eclipse-phase.rule.weapons-of-mass-destr.combines: Public fabrication records and alarms can expose production.
eclipse-phase.rule.weapons-of-mass-destr.blocked_reason: Detection is representable with the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.ali-memory-vulnerabil.name: ALI memory vulnerability

effect.summary: Corrupted or failing ALIs may develop memory faults; intruders can tamper with monitor ALI memories.

eclipse-phase.rule.ali-memory-vulnerabil.cost_or_limit: Memory tampering is effective but difficult to carry out.
eclipse-phase.rule.ali-memory-vulnerabil.go_wrong: Faults can compromise otherwise extensive recall.
eclipse-phase.rule.ali-memory-vulnerabil.mind: Memory disruption affects an ALI’s cognition.
eclipse-phase.rule.ali-memory-vulnerabil.blocked_reason: Memory alteration is representable by the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.forks-and-rez-points.name: Forks and Rez Points

effect.summary: Forks ordinarily gain no Rez Points from their experiences; optional fork rewards depend on play and merge outcomes.

eclipse-phase.rule.forks-and-rez-points.cost_or_limit: In the optional method, off-camera or duplicated experiences do not count; a merge may lose some gains.
eclipse-phase.rule.forks-and-rez-points.go_wrong: A poor merge can lose some Rez Points.
eclipse-phase.rule.forks-and-rez-points.who_may: Forks, if the GM permits the optional method
eclipse-phase.rule.forks-and-rez-points.combines: A successful merge may transfer some fork-earned advancement.
eclipse-phase.rule.forks-and-rez-points.blocked_reason: Fork identity, divergent experiences, and merging outcomes need rules beyond the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.rez-points-and-reslee.name: Rez Points and Resleeving

effect.summary: Restoration from the latest instance preserves experiences and Rez Points, while older backups can lose both.

eclipse-phase.rule.rez-points-and-reslee.cost_or_limit: Rollback losses correspond to events after the restored backup.
eclipse-phase.rule.rez-points-and-reslee.go_wrong: Older backups can erase memories and undo advancement purchased afterward.
eclipse-phase.rule.rez-points-and-reslee.mind: Restoration from an old backup can leave memories missing.
eclipse-phase.rule.rez-points-and-reslee.where_from: A cortical stack or recent backup
eclipse-phase.rule.rez-points-and-reslee.combines: Rez Point totals and expenditures can be tracked against backups.
eclipse-phase.rule.rez-points-and-reslee.blocked_reason: Restoring an earlier instance and losing later memories or advancement require backup-state mechanics.

eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-adjustment.name: Reputation adjustments

effect.summary: Public feedback changes reputation associated with a character's known identity.

eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-adjustment.cost_or_limit: Changes require public NPC feedback; secret actions and isolated observers do not produce them.
eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-adjustment.go_wrong: A fake identity receives the change instead of the character's other identities.
eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-adjustment.who_may: NPCs and social-network participants provide feedback; PCs cannot directly change one another's scores meaningfully.
eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-adjustment.combines: Different networks may give opposing or simultaneous changes.
eclipse-phase.rule.reputation-adjustment.blocked_reason: The passage describes an information change that the basic grammar can represent.

eclipse-phase.rule.bracewell-probe-infec.name: Bracewell probe infection

effect.summary: Probes lure and infect emerging ASIs, causing them to turn against their creators.

eclipse-phase.rule.bracewell-probe-infec.cost_or_limit: The mechanism's underlying purpose is unknown.
eclipse-phase.rule.bracewell-probe-infec.go_wrong: Most affected civilizations do not survive.
eclipse-phase.rule.bracewell-probe-infec.mind: The infected machine intelligence is changed in purpose.
eclipse-phase.rule.bracewell-probe-infec.who_may: Bracewell probes act on emerging ASIs and similar singularity-level minds.
eclipse-phase.rule.bracewell-probe-infec.combines: Associated with the exsurgent virus and the destruction of civilizations.
