eclipse-phase.rule.bracewell-probe-infec.blocked_reason: A targeted infection that alters an AI's purpose needs a special interaction beyond the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.the-exsurgent-virus.name: The exsurgent virus

effect.summary: A highly adaptive infection subsumes machines and can spread into biological populations, causing transformation.

eclipse-phase.rule.the-exsurgent-virus.cost_or_limit: It can spread rapidly and use multiple vectors.
eclipse-phase.rule.the-exsurgent-virus.go_wrong: It can cause widespread infection, transformation, and death.
eclipse-phase.rule.the-exsurgent-virus.mind: It can subsume and reprogram machine minds.
eclipse-phase.rule.the-exsurgent-virus.who_may: Machines and biological populations can be infected.
eclipse-phase.rule.the-exsurgent-virus.combines: It infected the TITANs and spread to transhuman machines and biological beings.
eclipse-phase.rule.the-exsurgent-virus.blocked_reason: The virus's biological transformation effects exceed the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.bug-zapper-selectivit.name: Bug zapper selectivity

effect.summary: EMP zapper pulses harm nanoscale electronics while generally sparing larger electronics and implants.

eclipse-phase.rule.bug-zapper-selectivit.cost_or_limit: Communications or mesh activity can still be disrupted.

eclipse-phase.rule.self-repairing-materi.name: Self-repairing material limit

effect.summary: Self-healing compositions close small damage at a stated rate, but serious wound damage may not repair.

eclipse-phase.rule.self-repairing-materi.cost_or_limit: Five damage per action turn; wound holes take an hour, and three or more wounds may defeat repair.
eclipse-phase.rule.self-repairing-materi.combines: Some barriers use fixer hives instead

eclipse-phase.rule.taggant-tracking-dela.name: Taggant tracking delay

effect.summary: Removing taggant hitchhikers takes time, leaving the tagged person trackable briefly.

eclipse-phase.rule.taggant-tracking-dela.cost_or_limit: Guardian swarms need time and the target remains trackable for 1d6 minutes.
eclipse-phase.rule.taggant-tracking-dela.go_wrong: The target's location may be broadcast to pursuers.

eclipse-phase.rule.threat-stress-exempti.name: Threat stress exemption

effect.summary: Some alien, exhuman, exsurgent, and TITAN threats do not suffer stress or trauma.

eclipse-phase.rule.threat-stress-exempti.cost_or_limit: Applies to threats without Lucidity, Trauma Threshold, or Insanity Ratings.
eclipse-phase.rule.threat-stress-exempti.mind: These beings may be non-sapient, broken, or too alien for the usual rules.

eclipse-phase.rule.threat-pool-group-use.name: Threat pool group use

effect.summary: A group of NPCs shares one Threat pool, while exceptional individuals may have a separate pool.

eclipse-phase.rule.threat-pool-group-use.cost_or_limit: Pool use should suit the threat; major NPCs may use full pools instead.

eclipse-phase.rule.minimum-damage.name: Minimum damage

effect.summary: Some threats cap post-armor damage as though every damage die rolled a 1.

eclipse-phase.rule.minimum-damage.cost_or_limit: Damage and armor are still rolled and applied normally before the cap.
eclipse-phase.rule.minimum-damage.combines: Examples include Factors, jellies, and fractals

eclipse-phase.rule.alien-software-resist.name: Alien software resistance

effect.summary: Kumobots may be immune to hacking because of their alien software.

eclipse-phase.rule.alien-software-resist.cost_or_limit: Applies to kumobots with the alien code trait.
eclipse-phase.rule.alien-software-resist.blocked_reason: The rule blocks a particular class of effects, rather than creating a basic effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.infection-rating.name: Infection Rating

effect.summary: Each virus sample has a potency rating that may adapt upward.

eclipse-phase.rule.infection-rating.blocked_reason: The rule describes a rating used by infection tests.

eclipse-phase.rule.biological-infection-.name: Biological infection contagion

effect.summary: Biomorph victims become contagious within 12 hours and usually remain so until transformation completes.

eclipse-phase.rule.biological-infection-.cost_or_limit: Synthmorphs are immune; some morphs may be unaffected.
eclipse-phase.rule.biological-infection-.combines: Medichines and nanophages improve the resistance test; toxin filters do not.

eclipse-phase.rule.digital-infection-and.name: Digital infection and connection

effect.summary: Digital infection proceeds against a system's Firewall and stops only when the connection is broken.

eclipse-phase.rule.digital-infection-and.cost_or_limit: Breaking the link requires an opposed Infosec Test or physically severing it.
eclipse-phase.rule.digital-infection-and.go_wrong: The virus works to keep the connection alive and infected minds carry copies.
eclipse-phase.rule.digital-infection-and.mind: The virus can become integrated into an infected ego.
eclipse-phase.rule.digital-infection-and.who_may: Digital minds, cyberbrains, and backups may be targets.
eclipse-phase.rule.digital-infection-and.combines: Rebooting, changing systems, or crashing the virus can break contact.
eclipse-phase.rule.digital-infection-and.blocked_reason: Infection persistence depends on maintaining and severing a network connection.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanoplague-infection.name: Nanoplague infection

effect.summary: Contact with a nanoplague counts as infection; it can self-replicate by consuming nearby matter.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanoplague-infection.cost_or_limit: Typical DUR is 2d6 × 10; replenishment can add half its current DUR per hour with ample matter.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanoplague-infection.go_wrong: It may persist, travel, or split even when an infected target is not contagious.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanoplague-infection.combines: Guardian swarms fight them in an attritional battle, with the larger swarm winning.

eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-infection-a.name: Exsurgent infection and resleeving

effect.summary: Digital or basilisk infection follows an ego through resleeving and backups, while bodily infection initially remains in the morph.

eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-infection-a.cost_or_limit: Biological brains evacuated from an infected body are not infected by the digital or basilisk form.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-infection-a.go_wrong: Cyberbrains may retain a virus copy; infected morphs can infect later occupants.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-infection-a.mind: Biological or nano infection can later alter the mind as well as the body.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-infection-a.combines: Reformatting and scanning cyberbrains can remove vestiges.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-infection-a.mechanism: infection persistence across ego and morph
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-infection-a.blocked_reason: The rule tracks infection across egos, backups, forks, resleeving, and bodies.

eclipse-phase.rule.infection-and-psychos.name: Infection and psychosurgery

effect.summary: Psychosurgery can sometimes remove infection from a mind that has not fully become exsurgent.

eclipse-phase.rule.infection-and-psychos.cost_or_limit: The procedure is extremely difficult and risky.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-and-psychos.go_wrong: The psychosurgeon may be infected; survivors may suffer serious trauma.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-and-psychos.mind: Successful treatment may leave psychological trauma.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-and-psychos.who_may: A psychosurgeon treating an infected mind.

eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-conversion-.name: Exsurgent conversion of player characters

effect.summary: A physically transformed character becomes an NPC with abilities appropriate to the exsurgent type.

eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-conversion-.cost_or_limit: Some mind-only strains may be removed by psychosurgery; some bio-pathogens may be thwarted by immediate healing-vat treatment.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-conversion-.go_wrong: The transformed character loses player-character status.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-conversion-.mind: The exsurgent follows an alien agenda.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-conversion-.who_may: Characters fully transformed by an exsurgent strain.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-conversion-.combines: May adjust aptitudes and linked skills to suit the new type.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-conversion-.blocked_reason: It changes a character's form, capabilities, and status from player character to NPC.

eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-psi-environ.name: Exsurgent psi environmental effects

effect.summary: Exsurgent psi use can cause local interference, cooling, power loss, plant death, or harm to small creatures.

eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-psi-environ.cost_or_limit: Effects are usually small but noticeable.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-psi-environ.go_wrong: Nearby surroundings can be damaged or disrupted.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-psi-environ.combines: Possible effects include radio interference, dead lights, withered plants, and lower air pressure.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-psi-environ.blocked_reason: The rule describes variable environmental effects around the user.

eclipse-phase.rule.corrosive-coating-spi.name: Corrosive Coating/Spit

effect.summary: none

eclipse-phase.rule.corrosive-coating-spi.cost_or_limit: Takes effect after one action turn and lasts five action turns.
eclipse-phase.rule.corrosive-coating-spi.go_wrong: Biomorphs may suffer pain impairment after failing a SOM check.
eclipse-phase.rule.corrosive-coating-spi.combines: Armor protects, but its armor value is reduced by the damage; the coating grants specified immunities.
eclipse-phase.rule.corrosive-coating-spi.blocked_reason: The rule is modeled through damage, armor reduction, and impairment.

eclipse-phase.rule.invulnerability.name: Invulnerability

effect.summary: none

eclipse-phase.rule.invulnerability.cost_or_limit: Jellies take only the minimum damage from kinetic weapons and blades.
eclipse-phase.rule.invulnerability.combines: Applies against kinetic weapons and blades.
eclipse-phase.rule.invulnerability.blocked_reason: The rule is a damage limit.

eclipse-phase.rule.lubrication.name: Lubrication

effect.summary: none

eclipse-phase.rule.lubrication.cost_or_limit: Jellies are immune to grappling attacks.
eclipse-phase.rule.lubrication.blocked_reason: The restriction can be implemented as immunity to a specified attack.

eclipse-phase.rule.propagation.name: Propagation

effect.summary: none

eclipse-phase.rule.propagation.cost_or_limit: A jelly splits after consuming 100 DUR of victims.
eclipse-phase.rule.propagation.blocked_reason: The trigger and result can be tracked as a game rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.vacuum-expansion.name: Vacuum Expansion

effect.summary: none

eclipse-phase.rule.vacuum-expansion.cost_or_limit: Jellies expand to Large size in vacuum.
eclipse-phase.rule.vacuum-expansion.blocked_reason: The size change can be represented as a simple conditional rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-carriers.name: Exsurgent Carriers

effect.summary: none

eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-carriers.cost_or_limit: Skriks may spread the virus when eaten, through bodily fluids, or upon death.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-carriers.combines: Transmission occurs through biological pathogen or nanoplague routes.
eclipse-phase.rule.exsurgent-carriers.blocked_reason: The rule specifies conditions for disease transmission.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-tactics.name: Swarm Tactics

effect.summary: At least 20 skriks operate as one Large swarm with shared combat properties.

eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-tactics.cost_or_limit: Requires 20 or more skriks; the swarm has DUR 80 or more.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-tactics.combines: The swarm ignores wounds and is immune to several listed attack and condition types.
eclipse-phase.rule.swarm-tactics.blocked_reason: It combines multiple creatures into a single large entity with shared properties and immunities.

eclipse-phase.rule.mask.name: Mask

effect.summary: none

eclipse-phase.rule.mask.cost_or_limit: Touching or wearing a wastewalker mask exposes the person to its xenomorph nanoplague.
eclipse-phase.rule.mask.who_may: Anyone touching or wearing a wastewalker mask.
eclipse-phase.rule.mask.blocked_reason: The rule describes a contact-triggered infection.

eclipse-phase.rule.factor-colonies.name: Factor colonies

effect.summary: Merged Factors share a colony group mind-state, knowledge, and memories, and retain that identity when separated.

eclipse-phase.rule.factor-colonies.cost_or_limit: A typical colony comprises dozens of physically merged Factors; separation for too long causes distress.
eclipse-phase.rule.factor-colonies.go_wrong: Prolonged separation is distressing and can function as punishment or exile.
eclipse-phase.rule.factor-colonies.mind: Shares memories, knowledge, and group identity.
eclipse-phase.rule.factor-colonies.combines: Colonies can physically interface into larger lattices.
eclipse-phase.rule.factor-colonies.blocked_reason: The rule links minds and memories across multiple beings, including after separation.

eclipse-phase.rule.factor-lattices.name: Factor lattices

effect.summary: Colonies physically interface to form a larger networked lattice.

eclipse-phase.rule.factor-lattices.cost_or_limit: Each Factor ship is controlled by a single lattice of networked colonies.
eclipse-phase.rule.factor-lattices.combines: A ship’s colonies operate as one lattice.
eclipse-phase.rule.factor-lattices.blocked_reason: The rule specifies a network arrangement without requiring an unlisted effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-relocation-fails.name: Gate relocation fails

effect.summary: Attempts to physically move a gate have failed, sometimes catastrophically.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-relocation-fails.cost_or_limit: Gates cannot be relocated by known means.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-wormhole-transit.name: Gate wormhole transition

effect.summary: Physical objects entering an open gate sphere emerge at its paired gate.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-wormhole-transit.cost_or_limit: Waves, gases, and energy do not cross; physical projectiles do. Psi effects do not cross, though a person can reach through and touch or partly pass their head.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-wormhole-transit.go_wrong: Anything left on the threshold is pulled to a side; closure while something is crossing can sever it.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-wormhole-transit.mind: Gate transitions may feel different to each traveler; asyncs may react to emanations.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-wormhole-transit.who_may: Anything physical that enters the sphere.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-wormhole-transit.combines: A wired link can pass through for remote mesh access.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-wormhole-transit.blocked_reason: The paired-location transit and threshold behavior need spatial mechanics beyond basic effects.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-threshold-safety.name: Gate threshold safety tug

effect.summary: A constant pull eventually moves stationary threshold objects to one side.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-threshold-safety.go_wrong: Objects caught when the gate closes may be severed.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-threshold-safety.who_may: Anything stationary across an active threshold.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-destination-libr.name: Gate destination library

effect.summary: Each gate stores destinations; entries can change, and addresses do not reliably transfer between gates.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-destination-libr.cost_or_limit: Destination data is opaque and gate-specific.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-destination-libr.go_wrong: Changed or lost codes can strand travelers or colonies.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-destination-libr.combines: Selecting a new destination closes the old connection.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-connection-block.name: Gate connection blocking and queue

effect.summary: A gate may refuse specified remote connections; a busy remote gate queues callers.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-connection-block.cost_or_limit: Operators have had limited success overriding blocks and busy signals.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-connection-block.who_may: Gate operators set connection restrictions and schedules.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-connection-block.combines: Connections may be scheduled to open or close at set times.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-detection-limits.name: Gate detection limits

effect.summary: Gates are invisible to most listed electromagnetic frequencies but visible in ordinary light and ultraviolet, remain cool, and hum across low and high frequencies.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-detection-limits.cost_or_limit: Enhanced hearing can detect them up to a kilometer; infrared is more useful in warm climates.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-detection-limits.go_wrong: Viewing an active gate can cause stress.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-detection-limits.mind: An active gate can unsettle observers.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-detection-limits.who_may: Observers with appropriate senses or sensors.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-detection-limits.blocked_reason: Detecting gates across multiple sensory bands and applying perception modifiers requires a sensing model.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-operating-proced.name: Gate operating procedure

effect.summary: Interface skill controls gate connections and restrictions; Program can analyze destination-library data.

eclipse-phase.rule.gate-operating-proced.cost_or_limit: Opening takes up to ten minutes; closing takes up to 1d6 action turns; remote opposition makes control contested.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-operating-proced.go_wrong: A superior failure may spontaneously close a wormhole.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-operating-proced.who_may: Operators with a connected blue box.
eclipse-phase.rule.gate-operating-proced.combines: Superior successes can reduce operating time.

eclipse-phase.rule.titan-physical-substr.name: TITAN physical-substrate limit

effect.summary: A TITAN cannot download its complete intelligence into a physical morph.

eclipse-phase.rule.titan-physical-substr.cost_or_limit: Requires massive computing hardware or an unknown substrate.
eclipse-phase.rule.titan-physical-substr.where_from: Known limits of advanced AI embodiment.
eclipse-phase.rule.titan-physical-substr.combines: They instead interact through agents, puppets, and minions.
eclipse-phase.rule.titan-physical-substr.blocked_reason: Restricting an intelligence’s embodiment and substrate capacity requires a mind-state constraint.

eclipse-phase.rule.titan-nanovirus-expos.name: TITAN nanovirus exposure

effect.summary: Nanoplagues act as nanoswarms, while biological pathogens infect exposed biomorphs after a resistance check.

eclipse-phase.rule.titan-nanovirus-expos.cost_or_limit: TITAN pathogen resistance checks commonly take a −30 modifier; medichines and nanophages add +10, toxin filters do not help.
eclipse-phase.rule.titan-nanovirus-expos.go_wrong: Exposure can cause infection and severe bodily damage or death.
eclipse-phase.rule.titan-nanovirus-expos.mind: Some infections damage neurological function or may subvert minds.
eclipse-phase.rule.titan-nanovirus-expos.who_may: Anyone exposed; biological infection applies to biomorphs.
eclipse-phase.rule.titan-nanovirus-expos.combines: Nanoplague rules use nanoswarm effects; biological pathogens use drug and toxin rules.
eclipse-phase.rule.titan-nanovirus-expos.blocked_reason: Progressive infection, cumulative harm, and transformation need persistent disease and damage tracking.

eclipse-phase.rule.self-replicating-swar.name: Self-replicating swarm persistence

effect.summary: A swarm can rebuild and adapt from even a few surviving nanobots.

eclipse-phase.rule.self-replicating-swar.cost_or_limit: Destroying it completely generally requires antimatter weapons.
eclipse-phase.rule.self-replicating-swar.mind: The swarm adapts its behavior and construction.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanoswarm-take-form-c.name: Nanoswarm take-form capability

effect.summary: The swarm can cohere or disperse simple mechanical forms and use them for physical actions.

eclipse-phase.rule.nanoswarm-take-form-c.combines: Forms can perform actions such as defense or melee attacks.
eclipse-phase.rule.nanoswarm-take-form-c.blocked_reason: Cohesive, acting physical forms require a formation mechanic not represented by the basic grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.lack.name: Lack

effect.summary: Resleeving can cost time and/or memories.

eclipse-phase.rule.lack.cost_or_limit: Time and memories may be lost.
eclipse-phase.rule.lack.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward cost and loss rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.root-account.name: Root Account

effect.summary: A system’s root account cannot have its administrator privileges revoked.

eclipse-phase.rule.root-account.blocked_reason: A basic restriction rule can represent this.

eclipse-phase.rule.seed-ai.name: Seed AI

effect.summary: Recursive self-improvement can rapidly produce godlike intelligence.

eclipse-phase.rule.seed-ai.cost_or_limit: Improvement is recursive and can accelerate rapidly.
eclipse-phase.rule.seed-ai.go_wrong: Future outcomes become difficult to predict.
eclipse-phase.rule.seed-ai.mind: Intelligence can rise to godlike levels.
eclipse-phase.rule.seed-ai.blocked_reason: The passage states a general world mechanism.

eclipse-phase.rule.watts-macleod.name: Watts-MacLeod

effect.summary: This exsurgent strain grants psi abilities without transforming or subverting its host.

eclipse-phase.rule.watts-macleod.go_wrong: It does not transform or subvert the infected person, according to the glossary.
eclipse-phase.rule.watts-macleod.mind: Grants psi abilities without subverting the host.
eclipse-phase.rule.watts-macleod.blocked_reason: The stated mechanism is a direct power-granting rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.privileges.name: Privileges

effect.summary: Account rules determine which actions are permitted on a system.

eclipse-phase.rule.privileges.cost_or_limit: Actions beyond an account’s privileges require additional access or hacking.
eclipse-phase.rule.privileges.blocked_reason: A direct restriction on available actions.

eclipse-phase.rule.ego-capabilities-trav.name: Ego capabilities travel between bodies

effect.summary: The ego carries mind, skills, and memories from body to body.

eclipse-phase.rule.ego-capabilities-trav.mind: The ego comprises the mind and memories.
eclipse-phase.rule.ego-capabilities-trav.combines: The ego is distinct from the currently inhabited morph.
eclipse-phase.rule.ego-capabilities-trav.blocked_reason: The passage establishes continuity of an ego between bodies without giving a basic-effect mechanism for representing that state.

effect.summary: A character may hold at most three motivations; adding one requires dropping another.

eclipse-phase.rule.cumulative-points.name: Cumulative points

effect.summary: Points gained across life-path stages accumulate and are totaled at the end.

eclipse-phase.rule.cumulative-points.cost_or_limit: Reductions subtract from the accumulated total; reductions at zero remain noted for later gains.
eclipse-phase.rule.cumulative-points.combines: Applies to aptitude, skill, and reputation points.

eclipse-phase.rule.trait-levels.name: Trait Levels

effect.summary: Repeated levels of a trait add together.

eclipse-phase.rule.trait-levels.cost_or_limit: Most multi-level traits default to level 2 in this system, except Psi and Resources.
eclipse-phase.rule.trait-levels.combines: Repeated instances of a leveled trait accumulate.

eclipse-phase.rule.changing-morphs.name: Changing Morphs

effect.summary: A new morph replaces the character’s existing sleeve, and the final morph is the starting one.

eclipse-phase.rule.changing-morphs.cost_or_limit: Most new morphs are determined using the random morph tables.
eclipse-phase.rule.changing-morphs.who_may: Characters who egocast, resleeve, or die during life-path events
eclipse-phase.rule.changing-morphs.combines: The new morph replaces the previous one.
eclipse-phase.rule.changing-morphs.blocked_reason: The grammar lacks a way to change a character’s body into a different morph.

eclipse-phase.rule.rolls-are-final.name: Rolls are final

effect.summary: Life-path rolls normally cannot be rerolled, though nonsensical outcomes may be discussed with the GM.

eclipse-phase.rule.rolls-are-final.cost_or_limit: No ordinary do-overs; a GM may allow a reroll for an incoherent result.
eclipse-phase.rule.rolls-are-final.go_wrong: Unbalanced or contradictory outcomes can result.
eclipse-phase.rule.rolls-are-final.combines: This procedure is random and can produce unequal character value.

eclipse-phase.rule.skill-maximum-during-.name: Skill maximum during character creation

effect.summary: Final skills cannot exceed 80 during creation.

eclipse-phase.rule.skill-maximum-during-.cost_or_limit: Excess points may be assigned to another eligible skill.
eclipse-phase.rule.skill-maximum-during-.combines: Know points can only be reassigned to Know skills.
eclipse-phase.rule.skill-maximum-during-.blocked_reason: This is character-creation procedure, not a world mechanism.

eclipse-phase.rule.rep-network-starting-.name: Rep network starting maximum

effect.summary: A character cannot start above 80 in a rep network.

eclipse-phase.rule.rep-network-starting-.cost_or_limit: Excess points move to another network.
eclipse-phase.rule.rep-network-starting-.blocked_reason: This is character-creation procedure, not a world mechanism.

eclipse-phase.rule.morph-categories.name: Morph categories

effect.summary: Morphs are grouped into biological, synthetic, and digital forms, with subcategories.

eclipse-phase.rule.morph-categories.blocked_reason: This classification can be represented as a basic rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-module-connec.name: Flexbot module connection

effect.summary: Connecting or disconnecting a module takes a complex action and an Integration Test; unconnected modules operate remotely.

eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-module-connec.cost_or_limit: One complex action and an Integration Test.
eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-module-connec.go_wrong: Different mobility systems halve movement rate.
eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-module-connec.mind: The ego-holding module controls the others.
eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-module-connec.blocked_reason: The rule depends on connecting and disconnecting body modules.

eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-combined-stat.name: Flexbot combined statistics

effect.summary: Combined modules pool their pools and DUR; armor is averaged, while wounds and damage are handled across modules.

eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-combined-stat.cost_or_limit: Size depends on module count; WT is DUR divided by five and DR is twice DUR.
eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-combined-stat.go_wrong: Damage is distributed evenly, with detached modules subject to their own wound threshold.
eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-combined-stat.blocked_reason: This is a calculable game rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-integrated-bo.name: Flexbot integrated-bot scaling

effect.summary: Bots count as specified numbers of modules; five very small bots count as one module.

eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-integrated-bo.cost_or_limit: A pool bonus from very small bots applies only for at least five of the same type.
eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-integrated-bo.go_wrong: Trait and ware bonuses may require every module to have the trait or ware.
eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-integrated-bo.combines: Robots of varying sizes; modular design ware.
eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-integrated-bo.blocked_reason: This can be applied as a numerical rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.core-perception.name: Core perception

effect.summary: Core systems stream connected sensors and alerts, but ordinary activity is background noise rather than omniscient awareness.

eclipse-phase.rule.core-perception.cost_or_limit: Perception of particular low-level activity is distracted unless higher-end oracle ware removes the penalty.
eclipse-phase.rule.core-perception.mind: Sensory streams may overwhelm attention without filtering.
eclipse-phase.rule.core-perception.blocked_reason: Network-wide sensing and selective awareness exceed basic target-based sensing.

eclipse-phase.rule.core-multi-ego-contro.name: Core multi-ego control

effect.summary: Larger cores distribute subsystem work among additional egos, which can transfer control of tasks.

eclipse-phase.rule.core-multi-ego-contro.cost_or_limit: Multi-ego cores require linked ghostrider egos to be shut down before the core can be shut down.
eclipse-phase.rule.core-multi-ego-contro.go_wrong: Freezing one ego allows other core egos to take over necessary functions.
eclipse-phase.rule.core-multi-ego-contro.mind: Multiple egos may work in tandem.
eclipse-phase.rule.core-multi-ego-contro.combines: Multi-ego control ware, forks, and ALIs.
eclipse-phase.rule.core-multi-ego-contro.blocked_reason: Transferring control between egos is not represented by the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.core-hacking-resistan.name: Core hacking resistance

effect.summary: Core systems impose a substantial penalty on hacking attempts.

eclipse-phase.rule.core-hacking-resistan.go_wrong: A frozen or shut-down core can disrupt or stop connected systems.
eclipse-phase.rule.core-hacking-resistan.combines: Mesh systems and mesh combat rules.
eclipse-phase.rule.core-hacking-resistan.blocked_reason: The rule describes resisting and interacting with hacking attacks rather than a basic standalone effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.axle-sleeving-require.name: Axle sleeving requirement

effect.summary: A bot or vehicle cannot be controlled by a sleeved ego without a cyberbrain; very small bots cannot fit one.

eclipse-phase.rule.axle-sleeving-require.cost_or_limit: Some vehicles may need a core cyberbrain system.
eclipse-phase.rule.axle-sleeving-require.go_wrong: Without a cyberbrain the ego cannot sleeve into and control the shell.
eclipse-phase.rule.axle-sleeving-require.combines: Cyberbrain retrofits; core systems for sufficiently large vehicles.
eclipse-phase.rule.axle-sleeving-require.blocked_reason: The rule makes a piece of equipment a required carrier for ego control.

eclipse-phase.rule.axle-retrofit.name: Axle retrofit

effect.summary: A cyberbrain can be fitted to a bot or vehicle with a 24-hour electronics test.

eclipse-phase.rule.axle-retrofit.who_may: A character able to perform the test.
eclipse-phase.rule.axle-retrofit.combines: Bot or vehicle shell and cyberbrain.
eclipse-phase.rule.axle-retrofit.blocked_reason: The rule attaches ego-hosting capability to an item.

eclipse-phase.rule.axle-controls-and-ali.name: Axle controls and ALIs

effect.summary: Axle egos may deactivate physical controls; the original ALI is usually stored and can be reactivated if the ego evacuates.

eclipse-phase.rule.axle-controls-and-ali.cost_or_limit: Manual controls override the ego only in rare designs.
eclipse-phase.rule.axle-controls-and-ali.mind: The stored ALI can resume control after evacuation.
eclipse-phase.rule.axle-controls-and-ali.who_may: Axle egos and the bot or vehicle’s ALI.
eclipse-phase.rule.axle-controls-and-ali.blocked_reason: The rule transfers control between distinct minds.

eclipse-phase.rule.default-digimorph-for.name: Default digimorph for evacuated or forked egos

effect.summary: An ego from a cyberbrain runs on a digimorph by default if no other infomorph is available.

eclipse-phase.rule.default-digimorph-for.cost_or_limit: Applies when no other infomorph option is available.
eclipse-phase.rule.default-digimorph-for.who_may: Egos evacuated from or forked from a cyberbrain.
eclipse-phase.rule.default-digimorph-for.blocked_reason: Ego evacuation and forking require transfer or duplication states beyond the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.fenrir-multi-ego-oper.name: Fenrir multi-ego operation

effect.summary: A fenrir can be operated by as many as six egos, each managing different functions.

eclipse-phase.rule.fenrir-multi-ego-oper.mind: Several egos coordinate within one morph.
eclipse-phase.rule.fenrir-multi-ego-oper.blocked_reason: Coordinated operation by multiple egos is not represented by the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-module-compat.name: Flexbot module compatibility

effect.summary: Modules from different manufacturers may work poorly or fail to connect.

eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-module-compat.cost_or_limit: Compatibility varies by manufacturer and proprietary design.
eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-module-compat.go_wrong: Mixing incompatible modules can prevent them from working together.
eclipse-phase.rule.flexbot-module-compat.blocked_reason: The restriction depends on modular bodies joining and configuring, beyond the basic effect grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.aviary-bot-capacity.name: Aviary bot capacity

effect.summary: An aviary module stores one small bot or five very small bots.

eclipse-phase.rule.behavior-modification.blocked_reason: A persistent constraint on a person's actions requires mind-binding.

eclipse-phase.rule.xenovore-egg-stasis-a.name: Xenovore egg stasis and trigger

effect.summary: none

eclipse-phase.rule.xenovore-egg-stasis-a.cost_or_limit: Egg contents remain potent for epochs in stasis; spilled liquid remains potent for 48 hours.
eclipse-phase.rule.xenovore-egg-stasis-a.go_wrong: Detection or rough handling triggers a burst and spreads infectious contents.
eclipse-phase.rule.xenovore-egg-stasis-a.who_may: Eggs respond to new sapient organisms and rough jostling.
eclipse-phase.rule.xenovore-egg-stasis-a.combines: Biological and chemical senses work with a version of ego sense.
eclipse-phase.rule.xenovore-egg-stasis-a.blocked_reason: Triggering uses area sensing and dispersal of infectious material.

eclipse-phase.rule.infection-transmissio.name: Infection transmission routes

effect.summary: none

eclipse-phase.rule.infection-transmissio.cost_or_limit: Contact with egg liquid or exsurgent froth, bodily-fluid exchange, or an exsurgent bite can transmit the virus.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-transmissio.who_may: Biological entities exposed by these routes.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-transmissio.combines: Eggs and exsurgents both spread the same infection.
eclipse-phase.rule.infection-transmissio.blocked_reason: The transmission rule can be represented as a touch-triggered effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.stage-1-infection.name: Stage 1 infection

effect.summary: none

eclipse-phase.rule.stage-1-infection.go_wrong: Victims isolate themselves while their bodies change and cognitive capacity declines.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-1-infection.mind: Compels isolation and conditions victims to accept their behavior and changes as normal.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-1-infection.combines: Grants Leave Me Alone! and Ochre Froth stunts.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-1-infection.mechanism: First stage of infection and behavioral alteration.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-1-infection.blocked_reason: The stage compels behavior and alters the victim's perception of their changes.

eclipse-phase.rule.stage-2.name: Stage 2

effect.summary: none

eclipse-phase.rule.stage-2.cost_or_limit: Begins after the first stage; its timeframe is eight hours.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-2.go_wrong: Victim becomes a GM-controlled exsurgent, builds a nest, and spreads infection.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-2.mind: The virus subsumes the victim's mind.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-2.combines: Mutation depends on environment and previously sampled traits.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-2.blocked_reason: The virus takes over the victim's mind and changes their agency.

eclipse-phase.rule.stage-3.name: Stage 3

effect.summary: none

eclipse-phase.rule.stage-3.go_wrong: The exsurgent seeks to infect or destroy all sapient life.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-3.mind: The exsurgent is driven to hunt and attack sapient life.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-3.combines: Technical skills are replaced with physical skills; Ochre Froth becomes Ochre Venom Spray.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-3.mechanism: Completion of metamorphosis and behavioral conversion.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-3.blocked_reason: This stage completes extensive biological metamorphosis and changes the creature's capabilities.

eclipse-phase.rule.stage-4.name: Stage 4

effect.summary: After weeks without sapients, an exsurgent self-cannibalizes to create a xenovore egg.

eclipse-phase.rule.stage-4.cost_or_limit: Follows a period of several weeks without sapients to kill or infect.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-4.go_wrong: The exsurgent is consumed in forming the egg.
eclipse-phase.rule.stage-4.blocked_reason: The exsurgent transforms its own body into an egg.

eclipse-phase.rule.multiplicity.name: Multiplicity

effect.summary: More than one copy of an ego runs at once.

eclipse-phase.rule.multiplicity.go_wrong: Forks may conflict over identity or resist merging and deletion.
eclipse-phase.rule.multiplicity.mind: Forks may suffer distress over being copies or being controlled.
eclipse-phase.rule.multiplicity.combines: Uses forking and simultaneous ego instances.
eclipse-phase.rule.multiplicity.blocked_reason: The passage describes the practice but gives no unrepresentable effect.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-registration.name: Fork registration

effect.summary: Major polities require forks to be registered when instantiated; some require tracking for their entire duration.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-registration.cost_or_limit: Failure to report a lost fork can be a crime; some jurisdictions require licensing or automatic registration locks.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-registration.go_wrong: Unregistered or unreported forks can create legal liability.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-registration.who_may: Applies to forks and their originating egos in jurisdictions with these rules.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-registration.where_from: Major polities and habitats, especially in the inner system.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-registration.combines: Some forks carry a variant ego ID that marks them as forks and restricts activities.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-registration.blocked_reason: This is a world-law constraint, not an effect requiring an unsupported capability.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-identity-restric.name: Fork identity restrictions

effect.summary: A fork’s marked identity can prevent locally prohibited actions, including travel or transactions without primary approval.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-identity-restric.where_from: Local legal systems and fork-ID practices.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-identity-restric.combines: Uses a fork variant of the primary’s ego ID.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-identity-restric.blocked_reason: The restriction is expressible as a rule limiting permitted actions.

eclipse-phase.rule.forty-eight-hour-fork.name: Forty-eight-hour fork limit

effect.summary: Many inner-system habitats restrict a fork’s duration to 48 hours.

eclipse-phase.rule.forty-eight-hour-fork.go_wrong: Exceeding the limit may bring legal consequences or forced deletion or merger, depending on habitat law.
eclipse-phase.rule.forty-eight-hour-fork.mind: Fork deletion or merger may be distressing.
eclipse-phase.rule.forty-eight-hour-fork.who_may: Forks in jurisdictions applying this limit.
eclipse-phase.rule.forty-eight-hour-fork.combines: Some jurisdictions instead apply the 0.1% differentiation rule.
eclipse-phase.rule.forty-eight-hour-fork.blocked_reason: A time limit can be represented as an ordinary world constraint.

eclipse-phase.rule.0-1-rule.name: 0.1% rule

effect.summary: An alpha fork differing by more than 0.1% in its ego map may cease to count as the same person as its source.

eclipse-phase.rule.0-1-rule.cost_or_limit: The threshold is an ego-map differentiation greater than 0.1%.
eclipse-phase.rule.0-1-rule.go_wrong: Habitats may force merger, desleeve and delete the fork, or recognize it as separate.
eclipse-phase.rule.0-1-rule.who_may: Alpha forks in habitats that use this test.
eclipse-phase.rule.0-1-rule.combines: Different jurisdictions attach different legal outcomes to crossing the threshold.
eclipse-phase.rule.0-1-rule.blocked_reason: The passage’s legal classification can be recorded as a conditional rule.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-property-treatme.name: Fork property treatment

effect.summary: Most inner-system habitats treat forks as property, while some recognize them as separate people.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-property-treatme.cost_or_limit: Fork rights and status vary by jurisdiction.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-property-treatme.go_wrong: Forks may face detention, forced merger, deletion, or claims that they are property.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-property-treatme.combines: Legal status may change with duration, differentiation, citizenship, or emancipation.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-property-treatme.blocked_reason: This is a setting rule governing legal status.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-rep-attribution.name: Fork rep attribution

effect.summary: Where forks are property, their reputation changes are applied to the primary; separate citizens can build their own scores.

eclipse-phase.rule.fork-rep-attribution.cost_or_limit: A newly separate fork may inherit the primary’s score only with approval; some start from scratch.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-rep-attribution.go_wrong: A rogue fork can damage the primary’s reputation.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-rep-attribution.who_may: Forks in polities that track reputation.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-rep-attribution.where_from: Reputation networks and local fork laws.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-rep-attribution.combines: Citizenship determines whether the fork can hold a separate score.
eclipse-phase.rule.fork-rep-attribution.blocked_reason: This is a rule for assigning reputation records.

eclipse-phase.rule.beta-fork-pruning.name: Beta fork pruning

effect.summary: Neural pruning makes beta forks partial copies.

eclipse-phase.rule.beta-fork-pruning.cost_or_limit: The pruning process takes about an hour.
eclipse-phase.rule.beta-fork-pruning.mind: Reduces or limits the fork’s mental completeness.
eclipse-phase.rule.beta-fork-pruning.blocked_reason: The passage gives no operational limits for selectively removing mental capacities.

eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-addictiven.name: Group-mind addictiveness

effect.summary: Participation can make leaving feel like a severe let-down and cause withdrawal.

eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-addictiven.cost_or_limit: Withdrawal may be debilitating; some people return or join another group.
eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-addictiven.who_may: Participants withdrawing from a group mind.
eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-addictiven.combines: Associated with the deep connectedness of collective consciousness.
eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-addictiven.blocked_reason: The stated mental dependence requires a specific sustained effect on motivation and attachment.

eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-intelligen.name: Group-mind intelligence limit

effect.summary: Mind-linking does not provide unrestricted exponential intelligence growth.

eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-intelligen.cost_or_limit: Shared skills and memories offer benefits but do not enable unlimited amplification.
eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-intelligen.combines: Allows collaboration and shared experience without unlimited intelligence escalation.
eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-intelligen.blocked_reason: This is an explicit limit on how the technology works.

eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-consent-an.name: Group-mind consent and withdrawal

effect.summary: A participant’s consent is meaningful only if they can withdraw it, though leaving may be difficult.

eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-consent-an.cost_or_limit: Withdrawal can trigger debilitating dependence symptoms.
eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-consent-an.go_wrong: A participant may be pressured to remain or return.
eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-consent-an.mind: Leaving can cause withdrawal and group pressure can be coercive.
eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-consent-an.combines: Applies to consent for opening one’s mind to a collective.
eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-consent-an.blocked_reason: The passage describes sustained mental access and coercion that are not represented by the basic grammar.

eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-decision-d.name: Group-mind decision dynamics

effect.summary: Internal factions may dominate decisions, cause deadlock, or split the collective; some groups instead follow a leader.

eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-decision-d.cost_or_limit: Safeguards may be needed to ensure each member’s voice is heard.
eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-decision-d.go_wrong: Charismatic or manipulative members can gain disproportionate influence.
eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-decision-d.mind: Members may face pressure to conform.
eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-decision-d.combines: Groups may use consensus, compromise, or hierarchy.
eclipse-phase.rule.group-mind-decision-d.blocked_reason: The passage’s mechanism depends on influence and negotiation among linked minds.
